questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Erikson's psychosocial theory, a primary-school child (6–12 years) is working on the crisis of:
questions.e: Erikson places 6–12 year olds in 'industry vs. inferiority': children build competence through productive work and school success. Failure leads to feelings of inferiority.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Bronfenbrenner's microsystem of a child includes:
o: The child's family, school, peers and immediate setting
National education policy and cultural values
The parents' workplace and neighbourhood networks
questions.e: The microsystem is the child's immediate environment — family, classroom, peers and neighbourhood — where direct interactions shape development.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: According to Freud, the latency stage of psychosexual development spans approximately:
questions.e: The latency period (roughly 6 years to puberty) is when sexual impulses are dormant and energy is directed into school learning, friendships and social skills.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Gesell's maturational theory of development is best summarized by the idea that:
o: Social interaction is the only driver of growth
Environment alone decides when a child learns
Development unfolds on a biologically fixed timetable
Children must be drilled early to develop
questions.e: Gesell argued that maturation — the biological unfolding of the nervous system — sets the pace of development, so pushing skills before readiness is unproductive.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Montessori's 'absorbent mind' refers to:
o: A child's effortless, unconscious learning from the environment in early years
The teacher's ability to absorb all classroom noise
questions.e: Montessori described ages 0–6 as the 'absorbent mind' period, when children unconsciously and effortlessly soak up language, order and culture from their surroundings.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Spearman's 'g factor' in intelligence refers to:
o: General intelligence common to all mental tasks
questions.e: Spearman proposed a two-factor theory: 'g' (general intelligence) underlies performance on all cognitive tasks, plus 's' factors specific to each task.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Cattell's theory, fluid intelligence is:
o: Knowledge gained from schooling and culture
The ability to reason and solve novel problems
questions.e: Fluid intelligence is the capacity to think logically and solve new problems independent of acquired knowledge; crystallized intelligence is the knowledge-based counterpart.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Sternberg's triarchic theory does NOT include which type of intelligence?
questions.e: Sternberg proposed analytical, creative and practical intelligence. Musical intelligence belongs to Gardner's multiple intelligences, not Sternberg's triarchic model.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Thurstone identified how many primary mental abilities in his theory of intelligence?
questions.e: Thurstone proposed seven primary mental abilities — verbal comprehension, word fluency, number facility, spatial visualization, associative memory, perceptual speed and reasoning — rejecting a single 'g'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A child who scores high on Gardner's interpersonal intelligence is likely to be good at:
o: Understanding and working with other people
questions.e: Interpersonal intelligence is sensitivity to others' moods and intentions and the ability to work effectively with people — the 'people smart' strength.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The 'critical period' hypothesis in language development claims that:
o: Children need grammar drills before age 5
Language can be learned equally well at any age
There is an optimal window in childhood after which language learning becomes much harder
questions.e: The critical period hypothesis holds that the brain is maximally plastic for language in early childhood, making later acquisition noticeably harder.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Chomsky's Language Acquisition Device (LAD) is:
o: A hearing aid used in therapy
A hypothesized innate brain mechanism for learning grammar
questions.e: Chomsky proposed that children are born with a Language Acquisition Device — an innate capacity to extract grammatical rules from the speech they hear.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Kohlberg's conventional level of moral reasoning, a person obeys rules because:
o: They value social approval and law-and-order
questions.e: The conventional level (stages 3–4) is driven by conformity to social expectations, approval of others, and maintenance of law and order.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Carol Gilligan criticized Kohlberg's theory mainly because it:
o: Was based on male samples and undervalued care-based moral reasoning
Denied that children can reason morally
questions.e: Gilligan argued Kohlberg's stages reflected a male 'justice' orientation and overlooked the 'ethics of care' — responsibility and relationships — more common in women's moral reasoning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: McClelland's need for achievement (n-Ach) is strongest in people who:
o: Prefer easy tasks with guaranteed success
Prefer moderately challenging tasks with personal responsibility for outcomes
questions.e: High n-Ach individuals choose moderately difficult goals where effort matters, seek feedback, and take personal responsibility — the achievement-motivation profile.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: According to Alderfer's ERG theory, the three needs are:
questions.e: Alderfer condensed Maslow's hierarchy into Existence (material needs), Relatedness (social needs) and Growth (personal development) needs.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Herzberg's two-factor theory distinguishes between:
questions.e: Herzberg said hygiene factors (pay, conditions, supervision) prevent dissatisfaction, while motivators (achievement, recognition, growth) create genuine satisfaction.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Positive transfer of learning occurs when:
o: Learning in one situation helps learning in another
Old learning interferes with new learning
questions.e: Positive transfer is when previously learned knowledge or skills facilitate new learning, as when maths skills help in physics problem-solving.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Bilateral transfer of learning refers to:
o: Transfer of skill from one side of the body to the other
questions.e: Bilateral transfer is cross-education: practising a motor skill with one limb improves performance of the other, e.g., right-hand to left-hand writing practice.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The curve of forgetting, described by Ebbinghaus, shows that:
o: Forgetting is slow at first and fast later
Most forgetting happens soon after learning, then levels off
questions.e: Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve shows rapid loss of memory in the first hours after learning, tapering to a stable plateau — the basis for spaced revision.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which is the best classroom application of the forgetting curve?
questions.e: Because forgetting is fastest early, well-spaced reviews at expanding intervals (a day, a week, a month) lock material into long-term memory most efficiently.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Gestalt psychology, the principle of 'closure' means:
o: The mind fills in missing parts to perceive a whole
questions.e: Closure is the Gestalt tendency to perceive incomplete figures as complete wholes — the mind supplies missing contours to form a unified pattern.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Gestalt principle of proximity states that objects:
o: Must be identical to be grouped
Close together are perceived as a group
questions.e: Proximity means elements placed near each other are perceived as belonging together — a key law of perceptual organization.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Insight learning, studied by Köhler with chimpanzees, is best described as:
o: Sudden understanding of a problem's solution
questions.e: Köhler's apes showed insight — an abrupt 'aha' grasp of the whole problem structure (e.g., stacking boxes to reach bananas), distinct from slow trial and error.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Tolman's concept of 'latent learning' demonstrates that:
o: Learning can occur without reinforcement and appear later
questions.e: Tolman's rats explored mazes without reward and later used that hidden knowledge when food was introduced — proving learning can be latent until needed.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A 'cognitive map', in Tolman's theory, is:
o: A mental representation of spatial layout
questions.e: Tolman proposed that animals form cognitive maps — internal mental representations of environments — rather than mere stimulus-response chains.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In classical conditioning, extinction occurs when:
o: The conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented without the unconditioned stimulus
questions.e: Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus appears repeatedly without the unconditioned stimulus that originally produced the response.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Spontaneous recovery in conditioning refers to:
o: The reappearance of an extinguished response after a rest period
questions.e: After extinction, a conditioned response can briefly reappear after a pause — spontaneous recovery — showing the original learning was suppressed, not erased.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Thorndike's Law of Readiness states that learning is effective when:
o: The learner is mentally prepared and willing
questions.e: The Law of Readiness says a learner must be mentally set and motivated to act; forcing learning on an unwilling learner produces frustration and little learning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Skinner's operant conditioning, a variable-ratio schedule of reinforcement:
o: Rewards after an unpredictable number of responses
questions.e: Variable-ratio schedules (like gambling or fishing) reinforce after an unpredictable number of responses, producing the highest, most persistent response rates.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Negative reinforcement in Skinner's theory means:
o: Giving a zero in a test
Removing an unpleasant stimulus to strengthen a behaviour
questions.e: Negative reinforcement strengthens behaviour by removing something aversive — e.g., a headache disappearing when medicine is taken increases medicine-taking behaviour.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Shaping, in behavioural terms, is:
o: Reinforcing successive approximations toward a target behaviour
questions.e: Shaping builds complex behaviour by rewarding each closer approximation to the goal — the method used in animal training and skill instruction.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Premack principle states that:
o: A more preferred activity can reinforce a less preferred one
questions.e: The Premack principle (grandma's rule) uses a high-probability behaviour as a reinforcer for a low-probability one: 'finish your worksheet, then you can draw.'

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Bandura's social learning theory, 'vicarious reinforcement' means:
o: Learning by observing others being rewarded or punished
questions.e: Vicarious reinforcement is learning from the consequences others receive — a child repeats a behaviour after seeing a classmate praised for it, without being rewarded herself.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Self-efficacy, in Bandura's theory, is:
o: Belief in one's own capability to succeed at a task
questions.e: Self-efficacy is the learner's judgment of their own ability to perform a task; high self-efficacy raises effort, persistence and resilience after failure.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The strongest source of self-efficacy, according to Bandura, is:
questions.e: Enactive mastery — one's own successful experiences — builds self-efficacy most powerfully; mere persuasion or modelling are weaker sources.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Dewey's philosophy of education emphasizes:
o: Learning by doing through real-life experiences
questions.e: Dewey's pragmatism holds that education is life itself: children learn best by doing — experimenting, solving real problems and reflecting on experience.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Tagore's educational philosophy, embodied at Shantiniketan, stressed:
o: Harmony with nature, freedom and creative self-expression
questions.e: Tagore's Shantiniketan emphasized learning in nature's lap, freedom from rigid classrooms, and the development of the child's creative and spiritual personality.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Gandhi's Basic Education (Nai Talim) proposed that:
o: Learning should centre on productive craft and self-reliance
questions.e: Gandhi's Wardha scheme made a productive craft (like spinning or gardening) the medium of education, linking head, heart and hand toward self-reliant citizens.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Aurobindo's integral education aims at:
o: The harmonious development of body, mind and spirit
questions.e: Sri Aurobindo's integral education seeks the all-round unfolding of the child — physical, vital, mental, psychic and spiritual dimensions together.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In adolescence, the most prominent developmental task according to Havighurst is:
questions.e: Havighurst's developmental tasks for adolescence include emotional independence from parents, forming peer relations, and preparing for adult roles.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Egocentrism in Piaget's preoperational stage is illustrated when a child:
o: Believes everyone sees the world exactly as she does
questions.e: Preoperational egocentrism is the inability to take another's perspective — the classic three-mountain task shows children assuming others see what they see.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Animism in young children refers to the belief that:
o: Inanimate objects are alive and have feelings
questions.e: Preoperational children show animism — attributing life and intentions to inanimate things, e.g., saying the moon follows them or a stone is 'hurt'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Reversibility in Piaget's concrete operational stage means the child can:
o: Mentally reverse an action, like 3+4=7 so 7−4=3
questions.e: Reversibility is the ability to mentally undo an operation — understanding that addition and subtraction, or pouring and returning, are inverse processes.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Seriation, a concrete-operational ability, is the capacity to:
o: Arrange objects in a logical series, e.g., by size
questions.e: Seriation is ordering objects along a dimension such as length or weight — a concrete operational achievement emerging around age 7.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A formal-operational adolescent differs from a concrete thinker mainly in the ability to:
o: Reason hypothetically and systematically about abstract possibilities
questions.e: Formal operations bring hypothetical-deductive reasoning: adolescents can test 'what if' propositions systematically, like a scientist varying one variable at a time.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Vygotsky's concept of 'more knowledgeable other' (MKO) refers to:
o: Anyone — teacher, peer, parent — with greater understanding who guides the learner
questions.e: The MKO is anyone with a better understanding of the task — a teacher, an older student, even a peer — who supports the learner within the ZPD.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Private speech, in Vygotsky's theory, is:
o: Children's self-directed talk that guides their own thinking
questions.e: Vygotsky saw children's audible self-talk during tasks as private speech — a tool for self-regulation that later becomes silent inner speech.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: According to Piaget, language development is:
o: Largely a reflection of cognitive development
questions.e: Piaget held that thought precedes language: cognitive structures develop first, and language is one symbolic expression of that underlying cognition.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A teacher using 'reciprocal teaching' is applying ideas from:
questions.e: Reciprocal teaching — teacher and students taking turns leading dialogue on a text — is a scaffolded, social-constructivist strategy rooted in Vygotsky.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In the revised Bloom's taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl), the highest cognitive level is:
questions.e: The revised taxonomy reorders the top as Evaluating then Creating; 'Creating' (producing new work) is the highest-order cognitive process.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A test question asking 'Compare the water cycles of a desert and a rainforest' assesses which Bloom's level?
questions.e: Comparing two systems to find similarities and differences requires breaking material into parts and relating them — the Analyzing level.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which verb belongs to the 'Applying' level of Bloom's taxonomy?
questions.e: Applying involves using knowledge in new situations — verbs like demonstrate, solve, illustrate and use. Define/list are Remembering; evaluate is Evaluating.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In the affective domain (Krathwohl), the highest level is:
questions.e: Krathwohl's affective domain ascends from Receiving through Responding, Valuing and Organization to Characterization — where values consistently guide behaviour.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Simpson's psychomotor domain begins with which level?
questions.e: Simpson's psychomotor hierarchy starts with Perception (sensory awareness), then Set, Guided Response, Mechanism, Complex Response, Adaptation and Origination.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Dalton Plan, devised by Helen Parkhurst, is characterized by:
o: Individual assignments with contracts and freedom of pace
questions.e: The Dalton Plan gives students written assignment contracts to complete at their own pace, balancing individual freedom with teacher guidance.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Kindergarten method was founded by:
questions.e: Froebel founded the Kindergarten ('children's garden'), using gifts, occupations, songs and play as the natural medium of early learning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The project method of teaching was systematized by:
questions.e: Kilpatrick, a Dewey student, formalized the project method: purposeful, whole-hearted activity (like building a model village) carried out in a social setting.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In the heuristic method of teaching, the teacher's role is to:
o: Guide students to discover facts themselves
questions.e: H.E. Armstrong's heuristic method places the child as discoverer — the teacher arranges situations so learners find out rules and facts by inquiry.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The play-way method is most associated with:
questions.e: Caldwell Cook championed the play-way: learning through play and dramatic activity, arguing that play is the natural method of childhood learning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Micro-teaching was developed at:
questions.e: Micro-teaching — scaled-down 5–10 minute lessons to practise single skills with feedback — originated at Stanford under Dwight Allen in the 1960s.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which is NOT a core micro-teaching skill?
o: Skill of managing the school budget
questions.e: Micro-teaching skills include introducing, questioning, explaining, illustrating, reinforcement, stimulus variation and blackboard work — not budget management.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Flanders' interaction analysis, 'praising or encouraging' belongs to:
questions.e: Flanders classified accepting feelings, praising, accepting ideas and asking questions as indirect influence; lecturing, directing and criticizing are direct.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Herbartian five steps of a lesson plan are in the order:
questions.e: Herbart's formal steps: Preparation (readying minds), Presentation (new matter), Association (linking to known), Generalization (rules), Application (practice).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Morrison's unit approach to lesson planning emphasizes:
o: Mastery of a unit through exploration, presentation, assimilation, organization and recitation
questions.e: Morrison's teaching model organizes instruction around complete units with cycles of exploration, presentation, assimilation, organization and recitation for mastery.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A 'blueprint' in test construction is:
o: A table mapping objectives, content and question types for balanced coverage
questions.e: A test blueprint (table of specifications) ensures the paper samples objectives, content areas and difficulty levels in planned proportions — the mark of a valid test.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A diagnostic test is used primarily to:
o: Identify specific learning difficulties and their causes
questions.e: Diagnostic tests pinpoint the nature and causes of a learner's difficulties in a subject so remedial teaching can be precisely targeted.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: An aptitude test measures:
o: What a student has already learned
Potential to learn or succeed in a future task
questions.e: Aptitude tests assess capacity for future learning (e.g., teaching aptitude), while achievement tests measure what has already been learned.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Content validity of a test means:
o: The test adequately samples the content and objectives it claims to measure
questions.e: Content validity is established by expert judgment that test items representatively cover the syllabus and learning objectives.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The reliability of a test is most directly checked by:
questions.e: Reliability — consistency of scores — is estimated through test-retest, parallel forms, or split-half/internal-consistency coefficients.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A criterion-referenced test interprets scores by:
o: Comparing with a fixed performance standard
questions.e: Criterion-referenced tests judge each learner against preset mastery criteria (e.g., 80% correct), unlike norm-referenced tests that rank against peers.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A portfolio assessment is valuable mainly because it:
o: Shows a student's growth and best work over time
questions.e: Portfolios collect selected work samples over time, revealing progress, reflection and strengths that a single test cannot capture.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: An anecdotal record is:
o: A brief factual note of a significant observed behaviour
questions.e: Anecdotal records are short, objective descriptions of notable incidents — useful for understanding behaviour patterns and guiding counselling.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Sociometry in a classroom is used to:
o: Map social relationships and peer acceptance among students
questions.e: Sociometric techniques (e.g., 'name three classmates you'd like to work with') reveal friendship patterns, isolates and group structure.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A rubric differs from simple marking mainly in that it:
o: Describes quality levels for each criterion in advance
questions.e: A rubric spells out criteria and performance descriptors for each level, making assessment transparent, consistent and useful for feedback.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Action research by a teacher is:
o: Systematic inquiry by the teacher into her own classroom practice to improve it
questions.e: Action research is practitioner research: the teacher identifies a classroom problem, tries a change, observes results and reflects — a cycle of improvement.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The '5E' instructional model sequences learning as:
questions.e: The 5E constructivist model: Engage interest, Explore hands-on, Explain concepts, Elaborate with applications, Evaluate understanding.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In a flipped classroom, the typical arrangement is:
o: Lectures at home via video, active work in class
Homework in class, lectures at home via video
questions.e: Flipping moves direct instruction to pre-class videos, freeing class time for discussion, problem-solving and teacher-guided practice.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Cooperative learning is distinguished from simple group work by:
questions.e: True cooperative learning requires structured positive interdependence (sink-or-swim together) plus individual accountability — not just sitting in groups.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The jigsaw method of cooperative learning works by:
o: Making each student an expert on one part and teaching it to the group
questions.e: In jigsaw, each member masters one segment in an 'expert group', then returns to teach it to the home group — every piece is essential.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Differentiated instruction means the teacher:
o: Varies content, process or product to match learners' readiness and interests
Gives different syllabi to boys and girls
questions.e: Differentiation adapts what is taught, how it is taught, or how learning is shown, so all learners — from strugglers to advanced — progress.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The 'wait time' after a teacher's question should ideally be:
questions.e: Research (Mary Budd Rowe) shows 3–5 seconds of wait time sharply improves the length, quality and participation of student responses.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Probing questions by a teacher are used to:
o: Push a student to think deeper and justify an answer
questions.e: Probing follows up an initial answer with 'why?', 'give an example' or 'what if' — deepening reasoning rather than accepting surface responses.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Divergent questions in class are valuable because they:
questions.e: Divergent questions ('how many uses can you think of for...?') open many acceptable answers, nurturing creativity and flexible thinking.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A 'TLM' in Indian classrooms stands for:
questions.e: TLM = Teaching-Learning Material: charts, models, flashcards and manipulatives that make abstract ideas concrete.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Low-cost, no-cost TLMs are emphasized because they:
o: Can be made from local waste material and suit every school
questions.e: NCF and teacher-training stress TLMs from locally available, low-cost materials so every classroom — however poorly resourced — can teach concretely.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: SWAYAM is:
o: India's national MOOCs platform for free online courses
questions.e: SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) offers free online courses from school to university level, with certification options.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: NROER provides:
o: Open digital resources — audio, video, images — for school education
questions.e: The National Repository of Open Educational Resources hosts openly licensed digital materials mapped to the school curriculum.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: e-Pathshala, developed by NCERT and NIC, offers:
o: Free e-books, audio-video resources and periodicals for school education
questions.e: e-Pathshala is NCERT's free app/portal giving access to digitized textbooks, audio, video and supplementary readers.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Under NEP 2020, the new school structure replacing 10+2 is:
questions.e: NEP 2020's 5+3+3+4 design covers Foundational (5 yrs), Preparatory (3), Middle (3) and Secondary (4) stages aligned to children's developmental phases.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: NEP 2020's target Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education by 2035 is:
questions.e: NEP 2020 aims to raise higher-education GER from about 26% to 50% by 2035, including through expanded open and online learning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: According to NEP 2020, board examinations should be redesigned to test primarily:
o: Core concepts, critical thinking and application
questions.e: NEP calls for board exams that are easier, modular, and focused on conceptual understanding and higher-order skills rather than coaching-driven memorization.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE 2023) is organized around:
questions.e: NCF-SE 2023 draws on the Panchakosha concept of human development and details curricular goals for each NEP stage.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Bagless days, recommended by NEP 2020, are meant for:
o: Hands-on vocational exposure like internships with artisans
questions.e: NEP suggests 10 bagless days a year for Grades 6–8 for experiential vocational exposure — visits to artisans, farms and workplaces.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Vidya Pravesh programme is:
o: A 3-month play-based school-preparation module for Grade 1 entrants
questions.e: Vidya Pravesh, developed by NCERT, is a three-month play-based preparation module easing the transition from preschool/Anganwadi to Grade 1.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: NISHTHA training programme is meant for:
questions.e: NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement) is the large-scale integrated teacher-training programme under Samagra Shiksha.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan subsumes which earlier schemes?
questions.e: Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and Teacher Education into one school-education programme.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The main purpose of a 'morning assembly' in school management is:
o: Building community, values and communication skills
questions.e: Assembly nurtures school ethos — shared prayer, thought, news and announcements build belonging, values and public-speaking confidence.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A democratic school timetable is characterized by:
o: Flexibility with weightage to child needs and activity balance
questions.e: Good timetabling balances difficult and light subjects, includes activity periods and adapts to children's attention rhythms rather than rigid uniformity.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: During a Class 3 EVS lesson, Rani keeps asking 'why' questions that slow the lesson. The teacher's best response is to:
o: Send her out of the class
Praise her curiosity and use one 'why' as a class investigation
questions.e: Curiosity is the engine of EVS learning. Channeling one genuine 'why' into a brief class inquiry validates the child and teaches scientific thinking.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 5 student, Arjun, solves maths problems correctly but cannot explain his method. The teacher should:
o: Ask him to think aloud with a partner and model explaining
questions.e: Correct answers without explanation signal procedural fluency without conceptual articulation. Think-aloud and peer explanation build mathematical communication.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: In a Class 2 Hindi class, several children speak a regional dialect at home. The teacher should:
o: Accept the dialect and bridge it to standard Hindi
questions.e: NCF and NEP affirm the home language as a resource. Bridging from dialect to standard Hindi respects identity while building the target language.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Meena, a Class 4 student, cries whenever asked to read aloud. The most supportive first step is to:
o: Let her read to a small friendly group first and build confidence gradually
questions.e: Reading anxiety needs graduated exposure, not force or avoidance. Small-group reading lowers threat while keeping her practising.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Two Class 5 boys fight over a cricket ball during break. As class teacher, the best response is to:
o: Help them negotiate a turn-taking rule and reflect on fairness
questions.e: Conflict is a learning opportunity. Guided negotiation teaches conflict resolution and fairness; punishment alone teaches only avoidance.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A new student from another state cannot follow the medium of instruction. The teacher should initially:
o: Fail her in the first test
Use visuals, gestures and peer buddies while she acquires the language
Seat her alone at the back
Ask her to leave the school
questions.e: Language barriers need scaffolding — visuals, gestures and a buddy system — plus patience, not penal assessment of what she hasn't yet learned.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: During group work, one bright student does everything while others watch. The teacher should:
o: Assign clear roles to each member with individual accountability
questions.e: Structured roles plus individual accountability prevent free-riding and domination — the core design principles of cooperative learning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 1 child still sucks his thumb in class. The developmentally appropriate response is to:
o: Send him to a doctor immediately
Ignore it while providing engaging activities; it usually fades with involvement
questions.e: Thumb-sucking at 6 is usually self-soothing, not pathology. Engaging activities reduce it naturally; shaming creates anxiety.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Parents complain that homework is too heavy for Class 3. The teacher should:
o: Double the homework to show strictness
Review the load against NEP/RTE guidance and assign short, purposeful tasks
questions.e: NEP and NCERT discourage heavy homework in early grades. Short, meaningful tasks consolidate learning without burdening children or parents.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A visually impaired child joins Class 4. The most inclusive first step is to:
o: Seat him near the teacher, provide large-print/tactile materials and brief classmates
Ask parents to hire a tutor
questions.e: Inclusion means adapting the environment — seating, materials, peer sensitization — so the child participates fully, not separate treatment.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Class 5 students believe the Sun revolves around the Earth. The teacher's best move is to:
o: Elicit their reasoning, then use a model and observations to build the scientific view
Tell them they are wrong and move on
questions.e: Constructivist teaching surfaces misconceptions first, then confronts them with evidence and models — telling alone rarely changes deep beliefs.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A gifted Class 6 student finishes work early and disturbs others. The teacher should:
o: Send her to a higher class permanently
Give her more of the same drill
Provide enrichment tasks like open-ended projects
questions.e: Gifted learners need depth, not more drill. Enrichment — challenging, open-ended tasks — channels their energy productively.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: During a test, the teacher notices a usually honest student glancing at a neighbour's paper. The best response is to:
o: Quietly redirect her, and later discuss test purpose and integrity privately
questions.e: A private, non-shaming conversation addresses the behaviour while preserving dignity and opens a talk about learning vs. marks.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 3 student writes numbers mirror-style (like 3 as Ɛ). The teacher should:
o: Call it a learning disability at once
Give multisensory practice with formation; most reversals fade by age 7–8
Make him write 100 times as punishment
questions.e: Mirror writing is developmentally common in early grades. Multisensory formation practice resolves it; premature labelling harms.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Parents of a slow learner demand promotion be stopped. The RTE-compliant response is:
o: Explain no-detention with continuous support and remedial teaching
questions.e: RTE mandates no detention till Class 8 with continuous comprehensive evaluation; the answer is targeted remedial support, not retention.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 4 English lesson has 50 students of mixed levels. The best strategy is to:
o: Teach only to the middle level
Use pair work, graded tasks and peer tutoring
questions.e: Large mixed classes need pair work and tiered tasks so every child is engaged at her level — lecturing to the middle loses both ends.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A child from a nomadic family is irregular in attendance. The teacher should:
o: Keep her enrolled, provide bridge material and coordinate with parents
questions.e: RTE guarantees every child's right to education. Flexible bridge support keeps mobile children learning instead of pushing them out.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Students memorize the definition of 'photosynthesis' but cannot explain it. This shows:
o: Rote learning without understanding; the teacher should use experiments and diagrams
questions.e: Verbatim recall without explanation is rote learning. Simple experiments (e.g., destarching leaves) build the concept behind the term.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 2 teacher finds children restless after 20 minutes of sitting. She should:
o: Insert a short movement rhyme or activity break
questions.e: Young children's attention spans are short. Brief movement breaks restore focus — a developmental fact, not a discipline problem.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: In a science activity, a group breaks a borrowed thermometer. The teacher should:
o: Treat it as a learning moment about careful handling and safety
questions.e: Accidents in hands-on work are teachable moments about responsibility and safety; punitive responses kill the spirit of inquiry.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A shy Class 1 girl never speaks in class but talks freely at home. The teacher should:
o: Build trust through one-to-one talk, then small groups, before whole-class speaking
questions.e: Situational silence is usually anxiety, not inability. Graduated, low-threat speaking opportunities build confidence step by step.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Boys dominate the classroom discussion while girls stay silent. The teacher should:
o: Use structured turn-taking, wait time and directly invite girls' views
questions.e: Participation gaps need deliberate structures — equitable questioning, wait time, small-group rehearsal — not acceptance of the status quo.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 5 student asks a question the teacher cannot answer. The honest, pedagogically sound response is to:
o: Appreciate the question and explore the answer together
Scold the student for a tough question
questions.e: Admitting 'I don't know, let's find out' models intellectual honesty and turns the moment into collaborative inquiry.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: During EVS field observation, children start chasing butterflies instead of observing plants. The teacher should:
o: Briefly channel the interest — observe the butterfly-plant link — then refocus
questions.e: Children's spontaneous interests are pedagogical gold. Connecting butterflies to plants (pollination) enriches the lesson before refocusing.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 4 student consistently tops in tests but is lonely and bullied. The teacher should:
o: Work on social skills, peer pairing and address the bullying
questions.e: Academic success without social-emotional wellbeing is incomplete. The teacher must address bullying and scaffold peer relationships.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: The class laughs when a stammering child reads. The teacher must:
o: Stop the laughter firmly, sensitize the class, and give the child safe speaking chances
questions.e: Protecting the child's dignity comes first — firm, kind intervention plus class sensitization — then graded safe opportunities to speak.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A parent insists their Class 2 child should learn only English, not Hindi. The teacher should explain that:
o: Strong first-language foundations actually support second-language learning
questions.e: Research shows literacy in the home/first language transfers to second-language learning; suppressing it weakens both.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Students copy homework from each other daily. The most effective remedy is to:
o: Design homework that is personal, creative or discussion-based so copying is pointless
questions.e: Copy-proof homework — personal observations, family interviews, creative tasks — removes the incentive to copy while keeping practice meaningful.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 6 student is excellent at drawing but weak in studies. The teacher should:
o: Use her art talent as a bridge — diagrams, projects — while supporting academics
questions.e: Strengths are entry points, not distractions. Integrating art into learning builds confidence and motivation that lift academics too.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: During a maths test, a child solves using a novel method that works. The teacher should:
o: Mark it wrong for not following the taught method
Award full marks and invite the child to share the method
questions.e: Mathematics values valid reasoning over single methods. Celebrating alternative strategies deepens the whole class's number sense.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A new teacher faces a noisy Class 7. The most effective first strategy is to:
o: Establish a few clear routines and rules with the class, and engage them quickly
questions.e: Classroom management rests on predictable routines co-created with students plus engaging starts — authority built on respect, not volume.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A student with dyslexia struggles with a written test. A fair accommodation is to:
o: Give the same test with no change
Allow extra time and, where valid, oral responses
questions.e: Reasonable accommodations — extra time, oral alternatives — measure the student's knowledge rather than the disability, preserving validity.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Children bring junk food daily despite a nutrition lesson. The teacher should:
o: Involve families, run a food-diary project and model healthy eating
questions.e: Behaviour change needs home-school partnership and experiential projects, not confiscation — a food diary makes abstract nutrition personal.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 5 girl is withdrawn after her parents' separation. The teacher should:
o: Ask probing personal questions in class
Offer quiet support, routine stability and referral to the counsellor if needed
Discuss it with the whole class
questions.e: Emotional distress needs gentle, private support and stable routines, with counsellor referral for deeper needs — never public probing.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Students rush through activities to 'finish first'. The teacher should:
o: Shift praise from speed to quality, reflection and craftsmanship
questions.e: When speed is rewarded, learning suffers. Praising thoughtfulness and quality reorients the classroom culture toward mastery.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 3 teacher has no science kit. For a lesson on floating and sinking she should:
o: Use a tub of water with stones, leaves, coins and plastic lids
questions.e: Everyday materials make excellent science apparatus. A water tub with common objects teaches floating/sinking better than a diagram.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: An autistic student is distressed by sudden timetable changes. The teacher should:
o: Use visual schedules and give advance warning of changes
questions.e: Predictability reduces anxiety for autistic learners. Visual timetables and forewarning are evidence-based, respectful supports.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Class 4 students litter the classroom daily. The lasting solution is to:
o: Build ownership through class jobs, dustbins and reflection on shared space
questions.e: Responsibility is learned through ownership — rotating class jobs and reflection build lasting habits; punishment builds only evasion.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A bright student asks 'why do we need to learn this?' The teacher's best answer:
o: Connect the topic to real life and let students discover its uses
questions.e: 'Why learn this' is a legitimate demand for relevance. Linking content to real purposes builds intrinsic motivation; 'exam' answers kill it.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: During online class, most students keep cameras off and stay silent. The teacher should:
o: Use polls, chat, breakout rooms and short interactive tasks
questions.e: Passive online lectures breed disengagement. Frequent low-stakes interactions — polls, chat, breakouts — pull students into active participation.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 2 child cries on the first school day. The teacher should:
o: Send her home for a week
Allow a brief parent stay, comfort her, and engage her in play
questions.e: Separation anxiety is normal. A gradual transition — brief parental presence, comfort, playful engagement — builds school attachment safely.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Two groups present conflicting answers in a science debate. The teacher should:
o: Guide both to examine evidence and reach a reasoned conclusion
questions.e: The pedagogical goal of debate is evidence-based reasoning. Guiding students to weigh evidence teaches scientific temper.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A teacher realizes mid-lesson that students have not understood. She should:
o: Pause, diagnose with a quick check, and reteach differently
questions.e: Responsive teaching beats syllabus racing. A quick formative check plus reteaching with a new approach rescues the lesson.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 5 student finishes lunch but others are still eating; he starts disturbing them. The teacher should:
o: Provide a quiet 'early-finisher' corner with books or puzzles
questions.e: Staggered finishing needs planned provision. An early-finisher corner with engaging materials prevents disruption constructively.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Parents ask how to help a Class 1 child with reading at home. The best advice is:
o: Make the child memorize the alphabet only
Read aloud daily, talk about pictures, and let the child retell stories
questions.e: Daily read-aloud with conversation builds vocabulary, comprehension and love of reading — far more powerful than workbooks or tutors.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A student says 'I am bad at maths, I can never improve.' The teacher should:
o: Teach a growth mindset: ability grows with effort and strategies, and show her progress
questions.e: Fixed-mindset self-talk needs countering with evidence of growth — small wins, strategy teaching and effort-praise rebuild mathematical self-belief.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: The headmaster asks a teacher to finish the syllabus two months early for revision. The teacher should:
o: Explain that deep learning needs time; plan brisk but complete coverage with integrated revision
questions.e: Rushed coverage produces fragile learning. Professional judgment balances pace with mastery — brisk coverage with built-in revision serves students best.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A Class 4 class has children of three different religions. During a festival lesson, the teacher should:
o: Ask minority children to stay silent
Present all festivals respectfully as part of shared culture
questions.e: Inclusive festival teaching builds mutual respect and constitutional values; respectful presentation of all traditions is the secular classroom ideal.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: A student with hearing impairment sits at the back and misses instructions. The teacher should:
o: Seat her in front, face the class while speaking, and use visual cues
questions.e: Front seating, facing students while speaking, and visual supports are basic, effective accommodations for hearing-impaired learners.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Caselet: Children are excited about a stray dog that entered the school. The teacher can best use this to:
o: Teach compassion for animals, safety around strays, and link to EVS
questions.e: Real events are curriculum opportunities — a stray dog opens lessons on animal care, safety and EVS themes of living things.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of the following is a Rabi crop?
questions.e: Rabi crops are sown in winter (Oct–Nov) and harvested in spring — wheat, barley, gram and mustard. Rice, cotton and maize are Kharif (monsoon) crops.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Germination of a seed requires all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.e: Seeds need water, oxygen and suitable temperature to germinate; sunlight is not required until the seedling emerges and begins photosynthesis.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The process by which plants make food is called photosynthesis. It mainly occurs in the:
questions.e: Leaves contain chlorophyll that traps sunlight, enabling the plant to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose — the food-making process.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A cactus has spines instead of leaves mainly to:
o: Reduce water loss in dry deserts
questions.e: In deserts, leaves are modified into spines to minimize transpiration (water loss), while the fleshy stem stores water.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The lotus plant floats on water because its leaves have:
o: A waxy coating and air spaces
questions.e: Floating plants like lotus have waxy, water-repellent leaves and spongy tissues with air spaces that keep them buoyant.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which bird cannot fly?
questions.e: The ostrich is flightless — its wings are too small for its heavy body — but it compensates with powerful running legs.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Birds like ducks have webbed feet because they:
questions.e: Webbed feet act like paddles, helping ducks and swans swim efficiently in ponds and lakes.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A woodpecker's beak is adapted for:
o: Probing and chiselling wood for insects
questions.e: The strong, chisel-like beak of the woodpecker is designed to drill into bark and extract insects and grubs.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Migration of birds like the Siberian crane to India happens mainly in:
questions.e: Migratory birds escape harsh northern winters, arriving in India's wetlands (like Bharatpur) in winter for food and milder climate.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The main function of roots in a plant is to:
o: Absorb water and minerals and anchor the plant
questions.e: Roots anchor the plant in soil and absorb water and dissolved minerals, which travel up the stem to the leaves.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which part of the plant grows into a new plant in potato?
questions.e: Potato is a modified underground stem (tuber); its 'eyes' are buds that sprout into new plants — an example of vegetative reproduction.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The three states of water are solid, liquid and gas. Ice melting into water is an example of:
questions.e: Melting is the change from solid to liquid on heating. Evaporation is liquid to gas; condensation is gas to liquid; freezing is liquid to solid.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In the water cycle, water vapour cooling to form clouds is called:
questions.e: Condensation is when water vapour cools and changes into tiny droplets, forming clouds — the step before precipitation (rain).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.e: Solar energy is inexhaustible and renewable; coal, petrol and natural gas are fossil fuels that take millions of years to form.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Biogas is mainly produced from:
questions.e: Biogas (mainly methane) is produced by anaerobic decomposition of cow dung and organic waste in a biogas plant.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The layer of air around the Earth is called the:
questions.e: The atmosphere is the envelope of gases surrounding Earth. Hydrosphere is water, lithosphere is land, biosphere is the zone of life.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which gas do plants absorb for photosynthesis?
questions.e: Plants take in carbon dioxide through leaf pores (stomata) and release oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Air exerts pressure. Which everyday observation proves it?
questions.e: An inflating balloon resists and pushes back because air occupies space and exerts pressure — a simple classroom demonstration.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The main cause of seasons on Earth is:
questions.e: Earth's 23.5° axial tilt makes different hemispheres lean toward the Sun at different times of the year, causing seasons.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A lunar eclipse occurs when:
o: The Moon comes between Sun and Earth
Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
The Sun is hidden by clouds
questions.e: In a lunar eclipse, Earth lies between the Sun and Moon, casting its shadow on the Moon. A solar eclipse is the reverse alignment.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.e: Mars appears red due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface — hence the name Red Planet.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The largest planet in our solar system is:
questions.e: Jupiter is the largest planet, with a mass greater than all other planets combined and the famous Great Red Spot storm.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The pole star (Dhruva Tara) is useful for:
questions.e: The pole star lies nearly above Earth's North Pole, so it always indicates north — a natural compass for travellers.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: On a map, the top usually represents:
questions.e: By map convention, north is at the top (unless stated otherwise), shown by the north arrow or compass rose.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A scale on a map tells us:
o: The ratio between map distance and actual ground distance
questions.e: Scale converts map measurements to real distances — e.g., 1 cm = 1 km — making maps useful for navigation and planning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of the following is a community helper?
questions.e: Community helpers — doctors, teachers, police, farmers, postmen — provide services that keep the community healthy and functioning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The postman is important to the community because he:
questions.e: The postman connects people by delivering letters, parcels and money orders — a classic 'people who help us' EVS topic.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which festival is known as the festival of lights?
questions.e: Diwali, the festival of lights, celebrates the victory of light over darkness and is marked by diyas, sweets and fireworks.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Pongal is mainly celebrated in:
questions.e: Pongal is Tamil Nadu's harvest festival, thanking the Sun god for the rice harvest — similar to Bihu, Baisakhi and Onam elsewhere.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The national animal of India is the:
questions.e: The Bengal tiger is India's national animal, symbolizing strength and grace; the peacock is the national bird.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The national tree of India is the:
questions.e: The banyan (Ficus benghalensis) is India's national tree, revered for its longevity and vast canopy.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these is a balanced-diet component that builds the body?
questions.e: Proteins (from pulses, milk, eggs, meat) build and repair body tissues; carbohydrates give energy, vitamins protect from disease.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Deficiency of iron in the diet causes:
questions.e: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; its deficiency causes anaemia — low red blood cells, tiredness and paleness.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Deficiency of Vitamin D causes:
questions.e: Vitamin D helps absorb calcium for bones; its deficiency in children causes rickets — soft, bowed bones.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which method kills germs in drinking water at home?
questions.e: Boiling water for a few minutes kills disease-causing germs — the simplest household method of making water safe.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The 3Rs of waste management are:
questions.e: Reduce consumption, Reuse items, and Recycle materials — the 3Rs minimize waste and conserve resources.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Compost is made from:
questions.e: Composting decomposes kitchen peels and garden waste into nutrient-rich manure — turning waste into a resource.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these materials is biodegradable?
questions.e: Banana peels decompose naturally by microorganisms; plastic, glass and metal persist in the environment for decades or centuries.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A shadow is formed when:
questions.e: Shadows form when opaque objects block light, creating a dark region behind them — the basis of shadow-play EVS activities.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of the following is a simple machine?
questions.e: The lever (like a see-saw or crowbar) is one of the six simple machines that make work easier by multiplying force.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A magnet attracts:
questions.e: Magnets attract magnetic materials — iron, nickel, cobalt. Wood, plastic and paper are non-magnetic.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The two poles of a magnet are called:
questions.e: Every magnet has a north-seeking and a south-seeking pole; like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Sound travels fastest through:
questions.e: Sound needs a medium and travels fastest through solids (particles close together), slower in liquids, slowest in gases — and not at all in vacuum.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The sense organ for smell is the:
questions.e: The nose detects smells; the tongue tastes, skin feels touch, ears hear, eyes see — the five sense organs.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which animal is a mammal that lays eggs?
questions.e: The platypus (and echidna) are monotremes — mammals that lay eggs yet feed their young with milk.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A food chain always begins with:
questions.e: Food chains start with producers — green plants that make food — then herbivores, carnivores and decomposers.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Earthworms are called 'farmer's friends' because they:
o: Loosen soil and add nutrients through castings
questions.e: Earthworms aerate the soil with burrows and enrich it with castings, improving fertility — hence 'farmer's friends'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which soil type is best for growing cotton?
questions.e: Black (regur) soil retains moisture and is rich in nutrients, making it ideal for cotton — the Deccan's famous cotton belt.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Terrace farming is practised in:
questions.e: In hills, fields are cut into step-like terraces to slow water runoff and prevent soil erosion.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The face value of 7 in 4,758 is:
questions.e: Face value is the digit itself regardless of position — 7. (Place value would be 700.) A classic CTET distinction.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 3?
questions.e: A number is divisible by 3 if its digit-sum is divisible by 3: 4+5+1+2 = 12, which is divisible by 3.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The HCF of 12 and 18 is:
questions.e: Factors of 12: 1,2,3,4,6,12; of 18: 1,2,3,6,9,18. The highest common factor is 6.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The LCM of 4 and 6 is:
questions.e: Multiples of 4: 4,8,12…; of 6: 6,12…. The least common multiple is 12.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which fraction is the largest?
questions.e: Converting to twelfths: 3/4=9/12, 2/3=8/12, 5/6=10/12, 1/2=6/12. So 5/6 is the largest.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 0.75 expressed as a fraction in lowest terms is:
questions.e: 0.75 = 75/100 = 3/4 in lowest terms.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.e: 25% is one-quarter: 480 ÷ 4 = 120.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The ratio 15:25 in simplest form is:
questions.e: Dividing both terms by 5 gives 3:5.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: If 5 pencils cost ₹30, the cost of 8 pencils is:
questions.e: Unitary method: one pencil costs 30 ÷ 5 = ₹6; 8 pencils cost 8 × 6 = ₹48.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A train runs 60 km in 1 hour. In 2.5 hours it covers:
questions.e: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm is:
questions.e: Perimeter = 2(length + breadth) = 2(8+5) = 26 cm. (40 cm² would be the area.)

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The area of a square with side 9 cm is:
questions.e: Area of a square = side × side = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
questions.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry — each through a vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
questions.e: Any line through the centre divides a circle into mirror halves, so a circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A right angle measures:
questions.e: A right angle is exactly 90° — one quarter of a full turn.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: An angle greater than 90° but less than 180° is called:
questions.e: Obtuse angles lie between 90° and 180°; acute are below 90°, reflex above 180°.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The volume of a cuboid 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm is:
questions.e: Volume = length × breadth × height = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cm³.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 1 litre is equal to:
questions.e: 1 litre = 1000 millilitres — a core measurement conversion for primary classes.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: How many minutes are there in 3 hours?
questions.e: 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 2.5 kg expressed in grams is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The next number in the series 3, 7, 11, 15, … is:
questions.e: An arithmetic pattern adding 4 each time: 15 + 4 = 19.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Find the missing number: 5, 10, 20, 40, …
questions.e: Each term doubles the previous: 40 × 2 = 80.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.e: 29 has no divisors other than 1 and itself. 21 = 3×7, 27 = 3×9, 33 = 3×11.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The smallest prime number is:
questions.e: 2 is the smallest (and only even) prime. 1 is neither prime nor composite.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these is a composite number?
questions.e: 21 = 3 × 7, so it is composite; 13, 17 and 19 are prime.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The product of the first three prime numbers is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Round 4,768 to the nearest hundred:
questions.e: The tens digit is 6 (≥5), so round up: 4,768 → 4,800.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 36 × 25 can be computed mentally as:
questions.e: All are valid: 36×25 = 36×100÷4 = 900. Flexible strategies like this build number sense.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A bar graph is most suitable for:
questions.e: Bar graphs compare discrete categories; pie charts show parts of a whole; line graphs show trends over time.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In a pictograph, if one symbol stands for 5 mangoes, 4 symbols stand for:
questions.e: 4 × 5 = 20 mangoes — reading a pictograph's key is the core skill.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The mean of 4, 8, 6, 10, 2 is:
questions.e: Mean = sum ÷ count = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The median of 3, 7, 5, 9, 1 is:
questions.e: Ordered: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The middle value is 5.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The mode of 2, 5, 3, 5, 7, 5, 1 is:
questions.e: Mode is the most frequent value — 5 appears three times.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A die has faces 1 to 6. The probability of getting an even number is:
questions.e: Even faces are 2, 4, 6 — 3 out of 6 = 1/2.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which 3D shape has 6 faces, all squares?
questions.e: A cube has 6 identical square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A cylinder has how many circular faces?
questions.e: A cylinder has 2 circular faces (top and bottom) plus one curved surface.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which net folds into a cube?
o: Six squares in a straight row
A cross shape of six squares
questions.e: The cross (one central square with one attached to each side, plus one more) is a classic valid cube net; six in a straight row cannot fold into a cube.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Roman numeral for 49 is:
questions.e: 49 = 40 + 9 = XL + IX = XLIX.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which is the greatest: 0.5, 0.05, 0.55, 0.505?
questions.e: Comparing: 0.55 > 0.505 > 0.5 > 0.05. Place-value comparison of decimals is a key primary skill.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Rina pours 3/5 litre of milk into a jug and then adds another 2/5 litre. How much milk is in the jug now?
questions.e: Like denominators add directly: 3/5 + 2/5 = 5/5 = 1 litre.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A classroom library has 30 storybooks. Two-thirds of them are picture books. How many picture books are there?
questions.e: Two-thirds of 30 = (2 × 30) ÷ 3 = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 picture books.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A shopkeeper gives a 10% discount on ₹200. The selling price is:
questions.e: Discount = 10% of 200 = ₹20; selling price = 200 − 20 = ₹180.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Simple interest on ₹1,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which pair of numbers are co-prime?
questions.e: Co-prime numbers share no common factor except 1: 7 and 11 are both prime and share only 1.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The predecessor of the smallest 4-digit number is:
questions.e: Smallest 4-digit number is 1,000; its predecessor is 999.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: How many 3-digit numbers are there in all?
questions.e: From 100 to 999 inclusive: 999 − 100 + 1 = 900.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Dienes' theory of mathematics learning, the 'free play' stage means:
o: Children explore materials without rules before structured learning
questions.e: Dienes' six stages begin with free play — unstructured exploration of manipulatives — before games, searching for commonality, and formalization.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: According to NCF 2005, the main goal of mathematics teaching is:
o: Mathematization of thought — developing logical reasoning
questions.e: NCF 2005 states the higher aim of maths teaching is mathematization — the ability to think logically, abstract and solve problems.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The green pigment in leaves that traps sunlight is:
questions.e: Chlorophyll absorbs sunlight energy for photosynthesis and gives leaves their green colour.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which gas is released by plants during photosynthesis?
questions.e: Photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide and water and releases oxygen as a by-product.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The male part of a flower is the:
questions.e: The stamen (anther + filament) produces pollen — the male part; the pistil/carpel is the female part.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Pollination is:
o: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
questions.e: Pollination — by wind, water, insects or animals — is the transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma, enabling fertilization.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these plants reproduces through spores?
questions.e: Ferns (like mushrooms and mosses) reproduce via spores, not seeds — a non-flowering plant group.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The hardest working muscle group for breathing includes the:
questions.e: The diaphragm, a dome-shaped muscle below the lungs, contracts to draw air in — the chief muscle of breathing.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
questions.e: Adults have 206 bones (babies are born with about 300, many fusing during growth).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The largest bone in the human body is the:
questions.e: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Digestion of food begins in the:
questions.e: Digestion starts in the mouth, where teeth mechanically break food and saliva begins chemical digestion of starch.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The small intestine is important because:
o: Most digestion and absorption of nutrients happen here
questions.e: The small intestine completes digestion and absorbs nutrients into the blood through tiny villi.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Red blood cells are made in the:
questions.e: Bone marrow produces red blood cells, which carry oxygen via haemoglobin.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The normal human body temperature is about:
questions.e: Normal body temperature is about 37°C (98.6°F); fever is typically above 100°F.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which vitamin is made in the skin with sunlight?
questions.e: Sunlight triggers Vitamin D synthesis in the skin — essential for calcium absorption and strong bones.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of:
questions.e: Vitamin A maintains healthy eyesight; its deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Scurvy is caused by lack of:
questions.e: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy — bleeding gums and weak immunity; citrus fruits prevent it.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Goitre is caused by deficiency of:
questions.e: Iodine deficiency enlarges the thyroid gland (goitre); iodized salt prevents it.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these is a communicable disease?
questions.e: The common cold spreads from person to person (communicable); diabetes, cancer and anaemia are non-communicable.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Malaria is spread by:
questions.e: The female Anopheles mosquito transmits the Plasmodium parasite that causes malaria.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Dengue is spread by which mosquito?
questions.e: The Aedes aegypti mosquito, which bites in daytime and breeds in clean stagnant water, spreads dengue.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these purifies blood in the human body?
questions.e: Kidneys filter waste from blood and form urine; the lungs exchange gases.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The human heart has how many chambers?
questions.e: The heart has four chambers — two atria (upper) and two ventricles (lower).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Arteries carry blood:
questions.e: Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart; veins return it to the heart.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The skull protects the:
questions.e: The skull (cranium) is the bony case protecting the brain; ribs protect heart and lungs.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of the following is a herbivore?
questions.e: Cows eat only plants (herbivores); lions and eagles are carnivores; humans are omnivores.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Frogs breathe through their skin when:
questions.e: Frogs use lungs on land but can absorb oxygen through moist skin, especially underwater or during hibernation.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Camels can survive long in deserts mainly because:
o: Their humps store fat and they conserve water
questions.e: Camel humps store fat (energy reserve), and camels minimize water loss through concentrated urine and dry dung.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Polar bears stay warm in the Arctic because of:
o: Thick fur and a layer of fat (blubber)
questions.e: Dense fur plus insulating blubber keep polar bears warm; black skin underneath absorbs solar heat.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which adaptation helps fish live in water?
questions.e: Gills extract dissolved oxygen from water, and the streamlined body reduces resistance while swimming.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A tadpole breathes through:
questions.e: Tadpoles (young frogs) breathe through gills like fish; adult frogs develop lungs — an example of metamorphosis.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Solids have:
questions.e: Solid particles are tightly packed in fixed positions, giving solids definite shape and volume.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these is a mixture?
questions.e: Air is a mixture of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and other gases that can be separated physically.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Filtration is used to separate:
questions.e: Filtration separates insoluble solids (sand) from liquids; salt/sugar need evaporation as they dissolve.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Evaporation is faster when:
o: It is hot, windy and dry
questions.e: Heat, wind and low humidity all speed evaporation — the principle behind drying clothes on a hot breezy day.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which force pulls objects toward the Earth?
questions.e: Gravity is Earth's pull on all masses — why dropped objects fall and why we have weight.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Friction is:
o: A force opposing motion, useful for walking and gripping
questions.e: Friction opposes relative motion; without it we couldn't walk or hold things, though it also causes wear.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A seesaw is an example of which simple machine?
questions.e: A seesaw is a first-class lever with the fulcrum between effort and load.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A ramp is an example of:
questions.e: An inclined plane (ramp) reduces the effort needed to lift loads — used in wheelchair ramps and loading docks.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which energy source is non-renewable?
questions.e: Coal is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years; wind, sunlight and tides are continuously renewed.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A solar cell converts:
questions.e: Photovoltaic solar cells convert sunlight directly into electricity.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: White light is made of how many main colours?
questions.e: White light splits into seven colours — VIBGYOR (violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red) — as seen in a rainbow.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A rainbow is formed by:
o: Refraction and dispersion of sunlight by raindrops
questions.e: Raindrops refract and disperse sunlight into its seven colours, forming the rainbow arc.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.e: Convex mirrors give a wider field of view with smaller images — ideal for rear-view mirrors.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The unit of electric current is:
questions.e: Current is measured in amperes; voltage in volts, resistance in ohms, power in watts.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.e: Copper conducts electricity well (used in wires); rubber, wood and plastic are insulators.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: An electric fuse is used to:
o: Protect circuits by melting when current is too high
questions.e: A fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit during overloads, protecting appliances from damage.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The nearest star to Earth is:
questions.e: The Sun is Earth's nearest star; the next nearest is Proxima Centauri.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Moon's phases are caused by:
o: The changing portion of the Moon's sunlit side visible from Earth
questions.e: Moon phases occur as we see varying amounts of the Moon's sunlit half during its orbit (Earth's shadow causes only eclipses).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: It takes the Moon about ___ to orbit the Earth:
questions.e: The Moon orbits Earth in about 27.3 days — the basis of the lunar month.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The hottest planet in the solar system is:
questions.e: Venus, despite being second from the Sun, is hottest due to a runaway greenhouse effect trapping heat.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Harappan civilization is also known as the:
questions.e: The Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilization flourished around 2600–1900 BCE along the Indus river and its tributaries.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Great Bath was discovered at:
questions.e: The Great Bath — a watertight ritual tank — is the most famous structure of Mohenjo-daro in present-day Pakistan.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Lothal is famous as an ancient:
questions.e: Lothal in Gujarat had a dockyard, showing the Harappans' advanced maritime trade with Mesopotamia.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Vedas were composed during the:
o: Vedic period, after the Harappan decline
questions.e: The Vedas were composed after the Harappan decline (c. 1500–500 BCE), beginning with the Rig Veda.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The oldest Veda is the:
questions.e: The Rig Veda, a collection of hymns, is the oldest of the four Vedas and a key source of early Indian history.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in:
questions.e: Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya, overthrew the Nandas and founded the Mauryan Empire in 321 BCE.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the:
questions.e: The bloodshed of the Kalinga War (261 BCE) transformed Ashoka, who adopted Buddhism and dhamma as state policy.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Ashoka's edicts were mainly inscribed on:
questions.e: Ashoka communicated dhamma through edicts carved on rocks and pillars across the empire, in Prakrit using Brahmi script.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Arthashastra was written by:
questions.e: Chanakya's Arthashastra is an ancient treatise on statecraft, economics and governance from the Mauryan era.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Gupta period is called the Golden Age of India mainly because of:
o: Advances in science, arts and literature
questions.e: Under the Guptas (4th–6th century CE), India saw great achievements — Aryabhata's astronomy, Kalidasa's literature, and temple art.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Aryabhata is famous for:
o: Explaining that Earth rotates on its axis and work on zero/place value
questions.e: The 5th-century astronomer-mathematician Aryabhata explained Earth's rotation and advanced the decimal place-value system.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between:
