questions.e: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526 using artillery and cavalry tactics, founding Mughal rule in India.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Akbar's revenue minister who designed the zabt system was:
questions.e: Raja Todar Mal, Akbar's finance minister, created the systematic land-revenue assessment (zabt/dahsala system).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Taj Mahal was built by:
questions.e: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal (completed c. 1653).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Shivaji founded the Maratha Empire in the:
questions.e: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674, establishing Maratha swaraj against Mughal and Deccan powers.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Revolt of 1857 began at:
questions.e: Sepoys mutinied at Meerut on 10 May 1857 over greased cartridges, then marched to Delhi — sparking the first war of independence.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Rani Lakshmibai is associated with:
questions.e: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi became a legendary leader of the 1857 revolt, fighting the British till her death at Gwalior.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
questions.e: On 13 April 1919, General Dyer's troops fired on an unarmed gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, killing hundreds.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn after:
questions.e: Gandhi called off the movement in 1922 after violence at Chauri Chaura, staying true to non-violence.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Dandi March (1930) was a protest against:
questions.e: Gandhi's 240-mile march to Dandi to make salt defied the British salt monopoly, launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'Do or Die' was the slogan of the:
questions.e: Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) call at the launch of the Quit India Movement in August 1942.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: India became independent on:
questions.e: India gained independence on 15 August 1947; the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The first President of India was:
questions.e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad became India's first President in 1950; Nehru was the first Prime Minister.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is regarded as the:
questions.e: As chairman of the Drafting Committee, Ambedkar shaped the Constitution and is honoured as its chief architect.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with:
questions.e: The Preamble opens 'We the People of India…', declaring India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of the following is a Fundamental Right?
questions.e: The Right to Equality (Articles 14–18) is a Fundamental Right; the Right to Property is now only a legal right (Article 300A).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the:
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Article 51A listing ten Fundamental Duties of citizens.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Right to Education (Article 21A) covers children aged:
questions.e: Article 21A (86th Amendment, 2002) makes free and compulsory education a fundamental right for ages 6–14.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Panchayati Raj system was constitutionalized by the:
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions with regular elections and reservations.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The head of a Gram Panchayat is called the:
questions.e: The elected head of a Gram Panchayat is the Sarpanch (Mukhiya in some states like Bihar).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The minimum age to vote in Indian elections is:
questions.e: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age from 21 to 18.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Lok Sabha has a maximum strength of:
questions.e: The Constitution caps Lok Sabha membership at 552 (530 states + 20 UTs + 2 Anglo-Indian nominated, the last now discontinued).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Rajya Sabha is a:
o: Permanent house not subject to dissolution
questions.e: The Rajya Sabha is permanent — one-third of members retire every two years — while the Lok Sabha dissolves every five years.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
questions.e: The President appoints the CJI (by convention the senior-most Supreme Court judge) under Article 124.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The largest continent in the world is:
questions.e: Asia is the largest continent by both area and population.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The largest ocean in the world is the:
questions.e: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of Earth's surface.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The longest river in the world is generally considered the:
questions.e: The Nile (about 6,650 km) is traditionally regarded as the world's longest river, slightly ahead of the Amazon.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Ganga originates from:
questions.e: The Ganga rises at the Gangotri glacier (Gomukh) in Uttarakhand.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.e: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The standard meridian of India (82°30′E) passes through:
questions.e: Indian Standard Time is based on 82°30′E longitude passing near Mirzapur, UP — 5:30 hours ahead of GMT.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Thar Desert lies mainly in:
questions.e: The Thar (Great Indian Desert) lies mostly in western Rajasthan, extending into Pakistan.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The highest peak in India is:
questions.e: K2 (8,611 m) in the Karakoram is India's highest peak (in PoK); Kanchenjunga is the highest within undisputed Indian territory.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Deccan Plateau is mainly made of:
questions.e: The Deccan Traps are vast basalt lava flows, weathering into fertile black (regur) soil.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Western Ghats are also known as:
questions.e: The Western Ghats running along India's west coast are locally called the Sahyadri range.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The oldest mountain range in India is the:
questions.e: The Aravalli range (Rajasthan) is among the world's oldest fold mountains, far older than the young Himalayas.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Mawsynram, the wettest place on Earth, is in:
questions.e: Mawsynram in Meghalaya's Khasi Hills receives the world's highest average rainfall.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The 'Manchester of India' is:
questions.e: Ahmedabad earned the title for its historic cotton textile industry, like Manchester in England.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Bokaro Steel Plant is located in:
questions.e: Bokaro Steel Plant (SAIL) is in Jharkhand — part of India's steel-industry geography.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these is a Kharif crop sown in June–July?
questions.e: Paddy is the main Kharif crop sown with the monsoon; wheat, mustard and barley are Rabi crops.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
questions.e: Direct speech needs a comma after the reporting verb and the quoted words in single/double quotes with the period inside.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Identify the tense: 'She has been teaching since 2010.'
questions.e: 'Has been teaching' with 'since' marks an action continuing from the past to now — present perfect continuous.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correct article: '___ honest man'
questions.e: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so it takes 'an'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: 'He is good ___ mathematics.'
questions.e: The fixed collocation is 'good at' (a subject or skill); 'good in' is not standard.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correct form: 'Neither of the boys ___ come.'
questions.e: 'Neither' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'has'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Identify the part of speech of 'quickly' in 'She runs quickly.':
questions.e: 'Quickly' modifies the verb 'runs', describing how — the hallmark of an adverb of manner.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of 'The teacher praised the boy.':
o: The boy was praised by the teacher.
questions.e: Object becomes subject + be-verb (past) + past participle + by-agent: 'was praised by the teacher'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correct reported speech: She said, 'I am tired.'
o: She said that she was tired.
questions.e: In reported speech, present 'am' backshifts to past 'was', with 'that' optional.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which word is a synonym of 'ancient'?
questions.e: 'Ancient' means very old — its synonym is 'old'; antonyms are modern/new/recent.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which word is an antonym of 'brave'?
questions.e: 'Cowardly' is the opposite of brave; bold, courageous and heroic are synonyms.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The plural of 'child' is:
questions.e: 'Child' has the irregular plural 'children' — a common CTET vocabulary item.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which sentence uses the comparative degree correctly?
o: She is more taller than me.
questions.e: 'Taller' already carries comparison; 'more taller' is a double comparative error.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: 'The wind whispered through the trees.'
questions.e: Giving human action (whispering) to the wind is personification.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'As brave as a lion' is an example of:
questions.e: A comparison using 'as…as' is a simile; without 'like/as' it would be a metaphor.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Direct Method of teaching English emphasizes:
o: Oral communication without translation, using the target language only
questions.e: The Direct Method teaches entirely in English through demonstration and realia, banning translation — Berlitz's approach.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Grammar-Translation Method is characterized by:
o: Learning grammar rules and translating sentences
questions.e: GTM focuses on explicit grammar rules, vocabulary lists and translation between mother tongue and target language.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In Communicative Language Teaching (CLT), the primary focus is on:
questions.e: CLT prioritizes using language for real communication; accuracy develops through meaningful interaction, not drills.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Total Physical Response (TPR), by Asher, is based on:
questions.e: TPR has learners respond to commands with actions ('stand up', 'point'), linking language to motor activity — ideal for beginners.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A 'minimal pair' (e.g., pin–bin) is used to teach:
questions.e: Minimal pairs differ by one sound, training learners to hear and produce phonemic contrasts.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Skimming a text means:
o: Reading quickly for the general idea
questions.e: Skimming is rapid reading for gist; scanning is rapid reading for specific information.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'Portfolio assessment' in language teaching mainly evaluates:
o: A collection of the learner's work over time
questions.e: Language portfolios gather drafts, recordings and reflections, showing growth in all four skills over time.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Error analysis in language learning treats errors as:
o: Evidence of the learner's developing interlanguage system
questions.e: Errors reveal the learner's interim grammar (interlanguage) — diagnostic data for teaching, not misbehaviour.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fossilization in second-language learning means:
questions.e: Fossilized errors persist in the learner's output even after correction and exposure — a key SLA concept.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The 'silent period' in language acquisition refers to:
o: A phase when learners listen and understand before speaking
questions.e: Beginners often go through a silent period of receptive intake before they are ready to produce speech — normal and healthy.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: कक्षा 3 की शिक्षिका flashcards पर ‘गंगा’, ‘दौड़ना’, ‘खुश’ और ‘मैं’ लिखकर बच्चों से पूछती हैं — इनमें संज्ञा (noun) वाला शब्द है:
questions.e: ‘गंगा’ किसी नदी के नाम को दर्शाता है — व्यक्तिवाचक संज्ञा। ‘दौड़ना’ क्रिया है, ‘खुश’ विशेषण और ‘मैं’ सर्वनाम।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: बच्चा कहता है: ‘राम स्कूल गया। वह थका था।’ — इस dialogue में ‘वह’ शब्द व्याकरण की दृष्टि से है:
questions.e: ‘वह’ यहाँ ‘राम’ (संज्ञा) के स्थान पर आया है — पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम। संज्ञा के बदले प्रयुक्त शब्द सर्वनाम कहलाता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: स्कूल के garden में शिक्षक ने ‘लाल गुलाब’ दिखाया और पूछा — ‘लाल’ शब्द यहाँ क्या है:
questions.e: ‘लाल’ गुलाब की विशेषता बताता है, अतः गुणवाचक विशेषण है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: playground में बच्चे दौड़ रहे हैं। शिक्षक पूछते हैं — ‘दौड़ना’ शब्द व्याकरण में क्या कहलाता है:
questions.e: ‘दौड़ना’ किसी कार्य या गति को दर्शाता है, अतः क्रिया है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: वाक्य ‘सीता ने गाना गाया’ में ‘ने’ किस कारक का चिह्न है — blackboard पर चर्चा के बाद सही उत्तर है:
questions.e: ‘ने’ कर्ता कारक का परसर्ग है — काम करने वाले (सीता) के साथ प्रयुक्त होता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: newspaper की headline ‘सूर्योदय’ पढ़कर शिक्षक ने संधि-विच्छेद पूछा — ‘सूर्योदय’ का सही विच्छेद है:
questions.e: ‘सूर्योदय’ = सूर्य + उदय (अ + उ = ओ) — गुण संधि का उदाहरण।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: textbook के पाठ में ‘नीलकमल’ शब्द आया — इसमें समास है:
questions.e: ‘नीलकमल’ = नीला है जो कमल — विशेषण-विशेष्य का मेल, अतः कर्मधारय समास।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: homework में ‘प्रवेश’ शब्द का विश्लेषण करना था — ‘प्रवेश’ में उपसर्ग है:
questions.e: ‘प्रवेश’ = प्र + वेश — ‘प्र’ उपसर्ग है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: worksheet पर ‘मिठास’ शब्द देकर प्रत्यय पूछा गया — ‘मिठास’ में प्रत्यय है:
questions.e: ‘मिठास’ = मीठा + आस — ‘आस’ भाववाचक तद्धित प्रत्यय है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: storybook में वाक्य था — ‘मोहन अपनी माँ की आँखों का तारा है।’ इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
questions.e: ‘आँखों का तारा’ = अत्यंत प्रिय व्यक्ति — मुहावरे लाक्षणिक अर्थ देते हैं।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: folktale सुनाते हुए नानी ने कहा — ‘बंदर ने केले देखे तो उसके मुँह में पानी आ गया।’ इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
questions.e: ‘मुँह में पानी आना’ = किसी चीज़ को देखकर तीव्र इच्छा या लालच होना।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: library की किताब में ‘उन्नति’ शब्द आया — इसका विलोम है:
questions.e: ‘उन्नति’ का विलोम ‘अवनति’ है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: कविता में ‘सूरज’ शब्द बार-बार आया — बच्चे ने synonym पूछा। ‘सूरज’ का पर्यायवाची है:
questions.e: ‘रवि’ सूर्य का पर्यायवाची है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: notebook जाँचते समय शिक्षक ने ‘आशीर्वाद’ की वर्तनी पर गोला लगाया — शुद्ध रूप है:
questions.e: शुद्ध वर्तनी ‘आशीर्वाद’ है — ‘श’ के बाद ह्रस्व ‘इ’ आता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: morning-assembly में प्रधानाचार्य बोले — ‘कल विद्यालय में वृक्षारोपण होगा।’ इस वाक्य का काल है:
questions.e: ‘होगा’ भविष्य की क्रिया है — कार्य अभी होना बाकी है, अतः भविष्यत् काल।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: dictionary में ‘कब’ शब्द देखकर बच्चे ने वाक्य बनाया — प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य है:
questions.e: प्रश्नवाचक चिह्न (?) और प्रश्नसूचक शब्द वाला वाक्य प्रश्न पूछता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: chart पर वर्णमाला टाँगते समय बच्चे ने पूछा — ‘अयोगवाह’ कहलाते हैं:
questions.e: ‘अं’ और ‘अः’ अयोगवाह कहलाते हैं — न पूरे स्वर, न पूरे व्यंजन।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: railway-station के नामपट्ट ‘त्रिवेणी’ से शिक्षक ने पूछा — ‘त्र’ वर्ण है:
questions.e: ‘त्र’ = त् + र — संयुक्त व्यंजन है (क्ष, ज्ञ, श्र भी इसी वर्ग में)।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: पद्य (poem) पाठ पढ़ाते समय शिक्षक का मुख्य ध्यान होना चाहिए:
o: लय, भाव और सौंदर्यबोध का विकास
questions.e: पद्य शिक्षण का केंद्र भावानुभूति, लय और काव्य-सौंदर्य है — अर्थबोध के साथ रसानुभूति।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: role-play गतिविधि में बच्चे दुकानदार-ग्राहक बने — इससे भाषा शिक्षण में मुख्य लाभ है:
questions.e: रोल-प्ले में बच्चे वास्तविक जीवन जैसे संवाद बोलते हैं — सहज मौखिक अभिव्यक्ति विकसित होती है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: भाषा शिक्षण में 'सुनना-बोलना-पढ़ना-लिखना' क्रम कहलाता है:
questions.e: बच्चा पहले सुनता है, फिर बोलता है, तब पढ़ना-लिखना सीखता है — यही LSRW का स्वाभाविक क्रम है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: पठन (reading) कौशल बढ़ाने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त classroom गतिविधि है:
questions.e: मौन या सस्वर वाचन के बाद अर्थ-चर्चा से बोध-क्षमता और गति दोनों बढ़ती हैं।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: उपचारात्मक (remedial) शिक्षण शुरू करने से पहले शिक्षक को सबसे पहले करना चाहिए:
o: निदानात्मक परीक्षण से कठिनाई के कारण पहचानना
questions.e: उपचार तभी सटीक होगा जब निदान सही हो — पहले यह जानें कि बच्चा कहाँ और क्यों अटक रहा है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Under the RTE Act, 2009, private unaided schools must reserve what percentage of seats in Class 1 for disadvantaged children?
questions.e: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act mandates 25% reservation in entry-level classes of private unaided schools for children from disadvantaged groups.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The RTE Act prescribes a pupil-teacher ratio of:
questions.e: The RTE schedule prescribes PTR of 30:1 for primary (Classes 1–5) and 35:1 for upper primary (Classes 6–8).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: DIETs (District Institutes of Education and Training) primarily provide:
questions.e: DIETs are district-level institutions for elementary teacher education — D.El.Ed programmes and in-service training.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: NCERT is headquartered at:
questions.e: The National Council of Educational Research and Training, established 1961, is headquartered in New Delhi.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Kothari Commission (1964–66) recommended the:
questions.e: The Kothari Commission recommended a common school system and the 10+2+3 pattern, plus 6% of GDP for education.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Operation Blackboard (1987) aimed to:
o: Provide minimum essential facilities to every primary school
questions.e: Operation Blackboard sought to ensure every primary school had at least two rooms, two teachers and essential teaching materials.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Mid-Day Meal scheme was renamed in 2021 as:
questions.e: The Mid-Day Meal scheme was rechristened PM POSHAN (Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment) in 2021.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In NEP 2020, ECCE (Early Childhood Care and Education) covers ages:
questions.e: NEP 2020 treats ages 3–8 as the foundational stage continuum (preschool + Grades 1–2), the critical window for brain development.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'विद्यालय' शब्द में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.e: 'विद्या + आलय' में आ + आ मिलकर दीर्घ 'आ' बनता है; समान स्वरों के मेल से दीर्घ स्वर संधि होती है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'नरेश' (नर + ईश) में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.e: अ/आ के बाद इ/ई आने पर 'ए' बनता है — यही गुण संधि का नियम है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'सूर्योदय' (सूर्य + उदय) में संधि है:
questions.e: 'अ' के बाद 'उ' आने पर 'ओ' बनता है, अतः यह गुण संधि है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'गिरीश' (गिरि + ईश) में संधि है:
questions.e: समान स्वर इ + ई मिलकर दीर्घ ई बनाते हैं, अतः दीर्घ स्वर संधि है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'तथैव' (तथा + एव) में संधि है:
questions.e: 'आ' के बाद 'ए' आने पर 'ऐ' बनता है — यह वृद्धि संधि है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'परोपकार' (पर + उपकार) में संधि है:
questions.e: अ + उ = ओ, अतः यहाँ गुण संधि हुई है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'उल्लेख' (उत् + लेख) में संधि है:
questions.e: त् के बाद ल आने पर त् का ल में परिवर्तन व्यंजन संधि कहलाता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'निश्चय' (निः + चय) में संधि है:
questions.e: विसर्ग के बाद च/छ आने पर विसर्ग 'श्' में बदल जाता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.e: दुः + गा में विसर्ग का परिवर्तन विसर्ग संधि का उदाहरण है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'नीलकमल' में समास है:
questions.e: नील (विशेषण) + कमल (विशेष्य) — विशेषण-विशेष्य संबंध कर्मधारय समास है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'गंगाजल' (गंगा का जल) में समास है:
questions.e: 'गंगा का जल' विग्रह से षष्ठी तत्पुरुष स्पष्ट होता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'त्रिभुवन' में समास है:
questions.e: पहला पद 'त्रि' संख्यावाची है, अतः यह द्विगु समास है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'माता-पिता' में समास है:
questions.e: दोनों पद प्रधान हों और 'और' से जुड़ें तो द्वन्द्व समास होता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'पीताम्बर' (पीत है अम्बर जिसका) में समास है:
questions.e: विग्रह किसी तीसरे पद की ओर संकेत करता है, अतः बहुव्रीहि समास है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'यथाशक्ति' में समास है:
questions.e: 'यथा' अव्यय पूर्वपद है, अतः अव्ययीभाव समास है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'अनुशासन' में उपसर्ग है:
questions.e: 'अनु' उपसर्ग 'शासन' मूल शब्द से पहले जुड़ा है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'पठनीय' में प्रत्यय है:
questions.e: 'पठ्' धातु में 'अनीय' प्रत्यय जुड़कर 'पठनीय' बना है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'मिठास' में प्रत्यय है:
questions.e: 'मीठा' में 'आस' प्रत्यय जुड़कर 'मिठास' भाववाचक संज्ञा बनी है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'प्राचार्य' में उपसर्ग है:
questions.e: 'प्र' उपसर्ग 'आचार्य' शब्द से पहले जुड़ा है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'राम ने रावण को मारा' — 'ने' किस कारक का चिह्न है?
questions.e: भूतकाल के कर्तृवाच्य में कर्ता के साथ 'ने' चिह्न कर्ता कारक दर्शाता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'वह कलम से लिखता है' — 'से' किस कारक का चिह्न है?
questions.e: क्रिया के साधन ('कलम से') को करण कारक कहते हैं।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'गरीबों को दान दो' — 'को' किस कारक का चिह्न है?
questions.e: जिसके लिए कुछ दिया जाए वह संप्रदान कारक होता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'वह घर से निकला' — 'से' किस कारक का चिह्न है?
questions.e: अलग होने/निकलने के भाव में 'से' अपादान कारक का चिह्न है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'सूरज' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है:
questions.e: रवि, आदित्य, दिवाकर सूर्य के पर्यायवाची हैं; चन्द्रमा भिन्न वस्तु है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'अमृत' का विलोम शब्द है:
questions.e: अमृत (जीवनदायी) का विलोम विष (प्राणघातक) है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'आकाश' का पर्यायवाची है:
questions.e: गगन आकाश का पर्यायवाची है; शेष शब्द भिन्न अर्थ रखते हैं।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'उन्नति' का विलोम शब्द है:
questions.e: उन्नति (ऊपर उठना) का विलोम अवनति (गिरावट) है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'दुर्जन' (दुः + जन) में संधि है:
questions.e: विसर्ग के बाद 'ज' आने पर विसर्ग 'र्' में बदलता है — विसर्ग संधि।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'सज्जन' (सत् + जन) में संधि है:
questions.e: त् + ज = ज्ज व्यंजन संधि का उदाहरण है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'पुस्तकालय' (पुस्तक + आलय) में संधि है:
questions.e: अ + आ मिलकर दीर्घ 'आ' बनता है, अतः दीर्घ स्वर संधि है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'अत्याचार' (अति + आचार) में संधि है:
questions.e: 'इ' के बाद भिन्न स्वर आने पर 'य' हो जाता है — यण संधि।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'ईद का चाँद होना' मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
questions.e: यह मुहावरा लंबे अंतराल के बाद दिखने वाले व्यक्ति के लिए आता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'नौ दो ग्यारह होना' मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
questions.e: यह मुहावरा अवसर पाकर भाग जाने के अर्थ में आता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'अंगूठा दिखाना' मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
questions.e: अंगूठा दिखाना अस्वीकृति या मना करने का संकेत है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'कान' का तत्सम रूप है:
questions.e: तद्भव 'कान' का तत्सम रूप 'कर्ण' है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 'हाथ' का तत्सम रूप है:
questions.e: तद्भव 'हाथ' संस्कृत के 'हस्त' शब्द से विकसित है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: शुद्ध शब्द चुनिए:
questions.e: 'शीर्षक' में दीर्घ ई और र्ष का सही क्रम यही है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: शुद्ध वर्तनी वाला शब्द छाँटिए:
questions.e: 'आशीर्वाद' में दीर्घ ई और वर्णों का सही क्रम यही है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: प्रत्यक्ष विधि (Direct Method) की मुख्य विशेषता है:
o: लक्ष्य भाषा में ही संवाद और शिक्षण; मातृभाषा का निषेध
questions.e: प्रत्यक्ष विधि में शिक्षण लक्ष्य भाषा में ही होता है और अनुवाद वर्जित रहता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: संप्रेषणात्मक उपागम (Communicative Approach) सबसे अधिक बल देता है:
o: वास्तविक स्थितियों में संप्रेषण क्षमता पर
questions.e: इस उपागम का लक्ष्य भाषा का व्यावहारिक प्रयोग सिखाना है, न कि केवल नियम।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: त्रिभाषा सूत्र के अनुसार हिंदी भाषी राज्यों में तीसरी भाषा होगी:
o: दक्षिण भारत की कोई आधुनिक भारतीय भाषा
questions.e: 1968 के त्रिभाषा सूत्र में हिंदी भाषी राज्यों हेतु दक्षिण की आधुनिक भारतीय भाषा अपेक्षित है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: मौन वाचन का मुख्य उद्देश्य है:
o: अर्थग्रहण की गति और एकाग्रता बढ़ाना
questions.e: मौन वाचन में पाठक अर्थ पर ध्यान देता है, अतः गति व एकाग्रता बढ़ती है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: निदानात्मक परीक्षण का उद्देश्य है:
o: अधिगम कठिनाइयों के कारणों की खोज करना
questions.e: निदानात्मक परीक्षण 'क्यों नहीं सीख पा रहा' — इसका उत्तर खोजता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: उपचारात्मक शिक्षण दिया जाता है:
o: नया पाठ शुरू करने से पहले
निदानात्मक परीक्षण के बाद, कठिनाई दूर करने हेतु
questions.e: पहले निदान, फिर उसी कठिनाई का उपचार — यही तार्किक क्रम है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: स्किमिंग (skimming) पठन कौशल है:
o: पाठ का मुख्य भाव या सार शीघ्र ग्रहण करना
questions.e: स्किमिंग में पाठक सार पकड़ने हेतु तीव्र दृष्टिपात करता है।

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.e: The correct spelling is a-c-c-o-m-m-o-d-a-t-i-o-n — double c, double m.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'candid':
questions.e: Candid means straightforward and honest, which is closest to frank.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'ancient':
questions.e: Ancient means very old; its direct opposite is modern.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The idiom 'to bite the dust' means:
questions.e: The idiom comes from falling in battle — it means to fail or be defeated.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: One who can use both hands equally well is called:
questions.e: Ambi- (both) + dextrous (skilled with the hands) gives ambidextrous.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correct passive form of 'She writes a letter.':
o: A letter has written by her
A letter was written by her
A letter is wrote by her
A letter is written by her.
questions.e: Simple present passive uses is/am/are + past participle: is written.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correct reported speech for: He said, 'I am busy.'
o: He said that he was busy.
He told that he is busy
He said that I was busy
He said that he is busy
questions.e: With a past reporting verb, present simple shifts to past simple in reported speech.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'Neither of the answers ___ correct.'
questions.e: Neither is singular, so it takes the singular verb is.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: '___ honest man came to meet you.'
questions.e: Honest begins with a vowel sound, so it takes an.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'He is good ___ mathematics.'
questions.e: The fixed collocation is good at something.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'By next year, she ___ her degree.'
questions.e: 'By + future time' calls for the future perfect tense.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Identify the erroneous part: 'Each of the boys were given a prize.'
questions.e: Each is singular, so the verb must be was, not were.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'Scarcely had he entered ___ the bell rang.'
questions.e: Scarcely/hardly pairs with when; no sooner pairs with than.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The word 'ship' begins with which sound?
questions.e: The 'sh' digraph represents the /ʃ/ sound.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'transparent':
questions.e: Transparent lets light through; opaque blocks it.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'abandon':
questions.e: To abandon is to give up or leave behind.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'The committee ___ divided in its opinion.'
questions.e: A collective noun takes a plural verb when its members act individually.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these sentences is correct?
o: He is working here for five years
He has been working here since five years
He has been working here for five years.
He works here since five years
questions.e: 'For' marks a duration with the present perfect continuous; 'since' needs a starting point.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The idiom 'a piece of cake' means:
questions.e: The idiom describes something effortlessly easy.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A person who speaks many languages is called a:
questions.e: Poly- (many) + -glot (tongue) = speaker of many languages.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correct active form of 'The cake was baked by mother.':
questions.e: Simple past passive 'was baked' converts to simple past active 'baked'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the question tag: 'She can swim, ___?'
questions.e: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'He has been working here ___ five years.'
questions.e: 'For' marks a duration; 'since' marks a starting point.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'This is the ___ interesting book I have read.'
questions.e: The superlative 'most' follows the definite article 'the'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'If he ___ harder, he would pass.'
questions.e: The second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'rapid':
questions.e: Rapid and swift both mean fast.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'victory':
questions.e: Victory and defeat are direct opposites.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Pick the word with the correct spelling:
questions.e: Embarrass is spelt with double r and double s.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The idiom 'break the ice' means:
o: to start a conversation in a social situation
questions.e: The idiom means easing tension so that people talk comfortably.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'Neither he nor his friends ___ coming.'
questions.e: With neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject — friends.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'She is junior ___ me.'
questions.e: Junior, senior, inferior and superior take 'to', not 'than'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'The news ___ shocking.'
questions.e: News is an uncountable singular noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Choose the correct direct speech for: He said that he was tired.
questions.e: Backshift reverses here: 'was tired' in reported speech was 'am tired' in direct speech.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Fill in the question tag: 'Let us go for a walk, ___?'
questions.e: 'Let us…' takes the fixed tag 'shall we'.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which activity best develops speaking skill?
questions.e: Speaking grows through meaningful oral interaction, which role play provides.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In the communicative approach, learner errors are treated as:
o: a natural part of learning, to be addressed gently
a sign of carelessness to be punished
a reason to stop speaking activities
questions.e: The communicative approach sees errors as evidence of hypothesis-testing in learning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The best first step before teaching a poem is to:
o: arouse interest through discussion or pictures
questions.e: Pre-reading engagement builds the schema that makes the poem meaningful.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Skimming as a reading strategy is used for:
o: getting the general idea of a text
questions.e: Skimming trades detail for speed in order to capture the gist.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A diagnostic test in English is given mainly to:
o: identify the causes of a learner's difficulty
questions.e: Diagnosis precedes remediation; ranking is not its purpose.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Multilingualism in the language classroom should be:
o: used as a resource for learning
questions.e: NCF 2005 treats multilingualism as a resource, not a problem.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE) in languages includes:
questions.e: CCE covers all-round development, not just written performance.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The structural approach to teaching English emphasises:
questions.e: The structural approach builds language through systematically graded patterns.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Remedial teaching in English is most effective when it:
o: follows diagnosis and targets the specific gap
is given to the whole class
questions.e: Remediation must match the diagnosed difficulty, or the effort is wasted.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Portfolio assessment in language learning is valuable because it:
o: shows a learner's progress over time
questions.e: A portfolio collects evidence of growth across tasks and time.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The primary goal of extensive reading is:
o: reading for pleasure, fluency and vocabulary growth
questions.e: Extensive reading builds fluency through large amounts of enjoyable text.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Find the HCF of 14 and 35.
questions.e: Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14; of 35: 1, 5, 7, 35; the highest common is 7.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Find the LCM of 6 and 15.
questions.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30…; of 15: 15, 30…; the least common is 30.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Add the fractions 3/4 and 1/6.
questions.e: With common denominator 12: 9/12 + 2/12 = 11/12.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Write 0.6 as a fraction in lowest terms.
questions.e: 0.6 = 6/10, which reduces to 3/5.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: What is 15% of 200?
questions.e: 10% of 200 is 20 and 5% is 10, so 15% is 30.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 2:3 and sum to 50. The smaller number is:
questions.e: 2 + 3 = 5 parts; 50 ÷ 5 = 10 per part; the smaller is 2 × 10 = 20.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: An article bought for ₹200 is sold for ₹250. The profit percent is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A sum of ₹5,000 is invested at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. The amount after 2 years is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The next prime number after 20 is:
questions.e: 21 and 22 are composite; 23 has no divisors besides 1 and itself.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is:
questions.e: The interior angles of any triangle always sum to 180°.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The area of a rectangle 8 units by 5 units is:
questions.e: Area = length × breadth = 8 × 5 = 40 square units.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The circumference of a circle of radius 7 units (take π = 22/7) is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A ₹800 article is sold at a 15% discount. The selling price is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The average of 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20 is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: 2/5 expressed as a percentage is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A finishes a task in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together they finish it in:
questions.e: Combined rate = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6 of the task per day, so 6 days.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A train runs at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. The distance covered is:
questions.e: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Find the missing term: 7, 14, 28, __, 112.
questions.e: Each term doubles the previous one: 28 × 2 = 56.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A right triangle has legs of length 3 and 4. Its hypotenuse is:

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The sum of an even number and an odd number is always:
questions.e: Even + odd = odd, for example 4 + 5 = 9.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The place value of 5 in 5,432 is:
questions.e: 5 is in the thousands place: 5 × 1000 = 5000.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: How many quarters are there in a half? (1/2 ÷ 1/4)
questions.e: Dividing by 1/4 is the same as multiplying by 4: 1/2 × 4 = 2.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The perimeter of a square of side 9 units is:
questions.e: Perimeter = 4 × side = 4 × 9 = 36 units.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The volume of a cube of side 3 units is:
questions.e: Volume = side³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cubic units.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The measure of a right angle is:
questions.e: A right angle measures exactly 90°.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Simplify 7 × 8 − 6 using the order of operations.
questions.e: Multiplication first: 56 − 6 = 50.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which is the largest: 0.5, 0.05, 0.55, 0.505?
questions.e: Comparing place by place: 0.55 > 0.505 > 0.5 > 0.05.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Compute 12² − 11².
questions.e: 144 − 121 = 23. The difference of consecutive squares equals their sum: 12 + 11.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A child writes 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5. The teacher should first:
o: give twenty similar sums for practice
use fraction strips to show why denominators cannot be added directly
ask the child to memorise the rule
questions.e: The error shows adding denominators; a visual model rebuilds the concept instead of masking it.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Concrete–Pictorial–Abstract (CPA) sequence means:
o: moving from concrete objects to pictures to abstract symbols
questions.e: CPA builds understanding by bridging concrete experience to abstract symbols.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Dienes blocks are mainly used to teach:
questions.e: Dienes blocks model ones, tens and hundreds — the base-10 place-value system.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: NCF 2005 wants mathematics teaching to:
o: develop reasoning and problem-solving, not rote procedures
finish the syllabus as fast as possible
questions.e: NCF 2005 positions mathematics as reasoning; rote procedures defeat that goal.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The most formative assessment move in a maths class is:
o: observing learners' strategies and asking probing questions
questions.e: Formative assessment gathers evidence during learning to guide the next steps.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which number is divisible by both 3 and 4?
questions.e: 12 is divisible by 3 (digit sum 3) and by 4 (12 ÷ 4 = 3).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The process by which water vapour turns into tiny droplets (clouds) is:
questions.e: Condensation is vapour turning back into liquid droplets, which we see as clouds.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The main source of energy driving the water cycle is:
questions.e: Solar heat drives evaporation, which powers the whole cycle.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which gas do green plants absorb from the air for photosynthesis?
questions.e: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The part of a plant that absorbs water from the soil is the:
questions.e: Roots absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Every food chain starts with:
questions.e: Producers capture solar energy, so every food chain starts with them.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The decomposers in nature are mainly:
questions.e: Bacteria and fungi break down dead matter and recycle nutrients.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these is a Kharif crop?
questions.e: Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon; paddy is the classic example.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Rabi cropping season in India falls in:
questions.e: Rabi crops like wheat are sown in winter and harvested in spring.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Day and night are caused by:
questions.e: One rotation of the Earth takes about 24 hours, giving day and night.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Seasons occur mainly because of:
o: great changes in distance from the Sun
Earth's tilt as it revolves around the Sun
questions.e: The 23.5° tilt changes how directly sunlight strikes each hemisphere.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A family in which grandparents, parents and children live together is a:
questions.e: A joint family spans three or more generations under one roof.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The most appropriate approach to teaching EVS is:
o: learning from the child's immediate environment through activities
questions.e: EVS begins with the child's surroundings; inquiry beats rote learning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A field trip in EVS is most valuable when learners:
o: observe, record and discuss what they find
questions.e: Observation plus recording and discussion turns a trip into genuine inquiry.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The broad EVS themes in the NCERT syllabus include:
o: Family and Friends, Food, Shelter, Water, Travel
questions.e: NCERT organises EVS around these lived-experience themes.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which process skill is central to EVS inquiry?
questions.e: Observing, classifying, predicting and inferring drive EVS inquiry.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Drinking water can be made safer at home by:
questions.e: Boiling kills most pathogens — the simplest household purification method.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Ganga flows through which of these states?
questions.e: The Ganga enters Bihar and flows east right across the state.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Kosi is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because:
o: it frequently shifts course and causes floods
questions.e: The Kosi's shifting channels have caused devastating floods in north Bihar.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: India's national animal is the:
questions.e: The Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris) is India's national animal.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Birds migrate mainly in search of:
questions.e: Migration follows food availability and survivable temperatures.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Growing different crops in succession on the same land is called:
questions.e: Rotation preserves soil nutrients and breaks pest cycles.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which cooking fuel is considered the cleanest?
questions.e: LPG burns with far fewer pollutants than solid or liquid fuels.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In EVS assessment, a portfolio is useful because:
o: it shows growth across tasks over time
questions.e: Portfolios collect evidence of progress, suiting EVS's activity-based nature.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The best way to teach the theme of 'shelter' in EVS is to:
o: compare local house types and the reasons for their design
dictate the definition of a house
questions.e: Comparing real houses links materials, climate and needs — genuine understanding.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of these actions conserves water?
questions.e: A dripping tap wastes litres daily; fixing it is direct conservation.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Child development is best described as:
questions.e: Development follows broad sequences, yet each child's pace and path vary.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Piaget's pre-operational stage spans:
questions.e: Pre-operational thought (2–7 years) is symbolic but egocentric and irreversible.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A Class III child conserves number but not volume. Piaget would place the child in the:
questions.e: Conservation develops during the concrete operational stage (7–11 years).

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development refers to tasks a child can do:
questions.e: The ZPD is the gap between solo and assisted performance — where teaching works.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Scaffolding in teaching means:
o: doing the task for the child
temporary support that is gradually withdrawn
questions.e: Scaffolds hold up learning and then fade as competence grows.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Kohlberg's pre-conventional level of morality is driven by:
questions.e: Pre-conventional reasoning centres on consequences for the self.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Erikson's psychosocial crisis for adolescents is:
questions.e: Adolescents work out a stable identity; failure leaves role confusion.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Gardner's theory of multiple intelligences implies that teachers should:
o: offer varied entry points to learning
questions.e: Multiple intelligences call for multiple representations, not one channel.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Intrinsic motivation comes from:
o: interest and satisfaction in the task itself
questions.e: Intrinsic drive is internal; rewards and fear are extrinsic motivators.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Maslow's hierarchy suggests a hungry child will struggle to learn because:
o: basic needs must be met before higher engagement
questions.e: Physiological and safety needs form the base of Maslow's pyramid.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 recognises how many disabilities?
questions.e: The 2016 Act expanded the recognised disabilities from 7 to 21.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Dyslexia primarily affects:
questions.e: Dyslexia is a specific learning disability in reading, despite normal intelligence.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The most inclusive seating for a learner who uses a wheelchair is:
o: an accessible spot within the regular classroom
questions.e: Inclusion means participating in the same space, with the access needed.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Labels such as 'slow learner' are discouraged because:
o: it lowers expectations and becomes self-fulfilling
questions.e: Labels trigger expectancy effects; describe the need, not the child.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Formative assessment is best described as assessment:
o: of learning — it gives the final judgement
for learning — it guides the next teaching steps
questions.e: Formative evidence feeds back into teaching while learning is still underway.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A portfolio differs from a written test because:
o: it collects work samples showing progress over time
questions.e: Portfolios document growth across contexts; a test snapshots one moment.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE) covers:
questions.e: CCE looks at the whole child — cognitive development and beyond.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The RTE Act prescribes the pupil–teacher ratio at the primary stage as:
questions.e: The RTE Schedule prescribes 30:1 at primary and 35:1 at upper primary.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Under NEP 2020, the foundational stage covers:
questions.e: NEP 2020's 5+3+3+4 design begins with five years of foundational learning.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Bloom's 'evaluate' level asks learners to:
questions.e: Evaluation is higher-order thinking: justifying judgements against criteria.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A teacher who often asks 'why do you think so?' is promoting:
questions.e: Justifying one's reasoning builds analysis and evaluation.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: A Class V learner finishes early and disturbs others. The best response is to:
o: send the learner out of class
give an enrichment task that extends the learning
questions.e: Enrichment channels fast finishers productively instead of punishing their pace.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: An effective classroom question is one that:
o: only the teacher can answer it
it has more than one defensible answer
questions.e: Divergent questions invite reasoning; single-answer drills invite guessing.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Learning is most durable when learners:
o: connect new ideas to what they already know
questions.e: Meaningful learning anchors new knowledge to prior schemas.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The best evidence that teaching has worked is that:
o: learners can apply the idea in a new situation
questions.e: Transfer to new situations proves understanding beyond mere recall.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The UP Board's September 2026 assessment guidelines for Classes 9–12, aligned with NEP 2020 and PARAKH, require question papers to primarily test:
o: Speed of writing and handwriting quality
Conceptual understanding, critical reasoning, source analysis and logical presentation
Completion of the paper in the shortest time
questions.e: The competency-based framework shifts assessment from rote recall to higher-order thinking: understanding concepts, reasoning critically, analysing sources and presenting logically — the NEP 2020/PARAKH direction.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Schools selected under the PM SHRI scheme (13,092 selected by September 2026, ~90% of the 14,500 target) are expected to demonstrate:
o: Effective implementation of NEP 2020 through modern pedagogy, inclusion and holistic development
questions.e: PM SHRI schools are meant to be exemplar institutions showcasing NEP 2020 in practice — modern teaching methods, safe inclusive environments and 21st-century skills, not infrastructure alone.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The APAAR ID rolled out for school students (a 12-digit registry; ~1 crore generated in Madhya Pradesh by September 2026) is:
o: A digital academic identity consolidating a student's records, grade sheets and achievements
A bank account number for scholarship transfers
questions.e: APAAR (Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry) is NEP 2020's 'one nation, one student ID' — a lifelong digital academic profile that travels with the learner across institutions.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: PARAKH, the national assessment centre under NCERT established per NEP 2020, is responsible for:
o: Setting norms, standards and guidelines for student assessment and evaluation
Running model schools in every district
questions.e: PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) is the standard-setting body for assessments; boards and states design their competency-based papers to its benchmarks.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: After the Supreme Court's 2025 direction on TET for in-service teachers (following which CBSE reopened the CTET 2026 application opportunity in August–September 2026), the core professional rationale for requiring TET is to:
o: Assure minimum professional standards of teaching competence across schools
questions.e: TET as a mandatory eligibility test guarantees that everyone entering or continuing in the classroom meets a common baseline of pedagogical and subject competence — a quality-assurance measure, not a revenue or transfer tool.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: In eligibility-test administration (e.g., Bihar STET 2026 issued one in September 2026), a 'dummy admit card' is issued primarily so that candidates can:
o: Learn their final exam centre in advance
Verify their personal and application details and correct errors before the final admit card
questions.e: The dummy admit card is a verification copy: candidates check name, category, photo and academic details and correct discrepancies within the window, preventing disqualification over clerical errors.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: The proposal for a 'North East Knowledge System' at the Northeast Education Conclave 2026 (19 September) draws directly on which component of NEP 2020?
questions.e: NEP 2020's Indian Knowledge Systems component asks education to root itself in India's traditional knowledge — the proposed regional knowledge system is that idea applied to the Northeast's indigenous heritage.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: NEP 2020's 360-degree holistic progress card differs from a conventional report card mainly because it:
o: Reports progress across cognitive, creative, socio-emotional and physical domains with self, peer and teacher assessment
Carries only the final board marks
Is issued once in a lifetime
questions.e: The holistic report card moves beyond scholastic marks to multidimensional progress, with assessment by the student herself, peers and teachers — capturing the whole child, not just exam scores.

questions.subject: BPSC TRE
questions.q: On 29 September 2026, TRE-4 aspirants protesting in Patna demanded that candidates appearing for which examination also be allowed to participate in the BPSC TRE-4 recruitment?
questions.e: The aspirants gathered outside Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari’s residence seeking parity with STET-appearing candidates, who are already allowed.

questions.subject: BPSC TRE
questions.q: After 932 posts were added in September 2026, the total number of teacher vacancies under BPSC TRE-4.0 became:
questions.e: 493 posts were added for Classes 9–10 (now 4,370) and 439 for Classes 11–12 (now 16,540), taking the total to 32,388.

questions.subject: BPSC TRE
questions.q: For appointment as a Class 9–10 teacher under BPSC TRE-4.0, which eligibility test is mandatory?
questions.e: Secondary (Classes 9–10) posts require STET Paper-1; senior secondary (11–12) posts require STET Paper-2.

questions.subject: BPSC TRE
questions.q: The maximum age limit for unreserved male candidates under BPSC TRE-4.0 is:
questions.e: 37 years for unreserved males; 40 for BC/EBC and unreserved women; 42 for SC/ST candidates.

questions.subject: BPSC
questions.q: In September 2026 the BPSC received zero applications for 218 Head of Department posts in government polytechnics. These posts belonged to which department?
o: Department of Science, Technology and Technical Education
questions.e: The 218 HoD posts across 16 disciplines were advertised on 26 August 2025; with zero applications even after re-advertisement, BPSC returned the requisitions to the department.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: According to Vygotsky, the gap between what a child can do independently and what the child can do with guidance is called the:
questions.e: The ZPD is the range where learning happens with scaffolding from a teacher or peer; instruction should target this zone.

questions.subject: CTET
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of formative assessment?
o: A quick diagnostic quiz during a lesson to adjust teaching
questions.e: Formative assessment happens during learning and feeds back into teaching; summative assessment (boards, term-end) judges learning after the fact.

questions.subject: Teaching
questions.q: IIT Bombay's October 2026 recruitment of 30 counsellors is for which centre?
questions.e: 26 student counsellors and 4 senior counsellors on an ad hoc basis; applications close 17 October 2026.

questions.subject: Teaching
questions.q: For the student counsellor posts at IIT Bombay (October 2026), the minimum post-qualification experience required is:
questions.e: Senior counsellor posts need 10 years. Applicants need an MA/MSc in Psychology with 55%+, plus an age limit of 45 as of 9 October 2026.

questions.subject: Recruitment
questions.q: How many total posts are advertised under BPSC TRE 4.0 after the October 2026 revision?
questions.e: BPSC raised TRE 4.0 (Advt 15/2026) vacancies from 32,388 to 33,320 school-teacher posts (announced 7 October 2026). Applications: 25 September – 26 October 2026.

questions.subject: Recruitment
questions.q: What is the last date to apply for BPSC TRE 4.0?
questions.e: Online applications for BPSC TRE 4.0 close on 26 October 2026 (fee payment by 26 October 2026) at bpsc.bih.nic.in.

questions.subject: Eligibility Test
questions.q: When did BSEB release the second dummy admit card for Bihar STET 2026?
questions.e: BSEB released the 2nd dummy admit card for Bihar STET 2026 on 1 October 2026 (corrections 1–7 October 2026). The first dummy admit card had been released on 25 September 2026.

questions.subject: Recruitment
questions.q: Which teacher-training/eligibility qualifications are accepted for BPSC TRE 4.0?
questions.e: BPSC TRE 4.0 requires graduation/post-graduation in the subject plus B.Ed, STET, CTET or D.El.Ed — i.e., a recognised teacher-training/eligibility qualification.

questions.subject: Exams
questions.q: How many candidates qualified for the Junior Research Fellowship in the UGC NET re-examination (English, Commerce, Sociology) results of 2026?
questions.e: 824 qualified for JRF, 11,610 for Assistant Professor and 23,154 for PhD admission. The re-test was held 9-10 September 2026; results at ugcnet.nta.nic.in.

questions.subject: Education policy
questions.q: Tamil Nadu's revised school timetable released on 13 October 2026 provides physical education and co-curricular activities for how many days a week?
questions.e: School Education Minister Rajmohan released a revised timetable giving physical education and co-curricular activities five days a week, following students' demands for more physical activity time.

questions.subject: Education policy
questions.q: Odisha's 13 October 2026 Cabinet decision on free textbooks covers students of:
questions.e: Free textbooks were approved for about 28.7 lakh students of Classes 9 and 10 in government and aided secondary schools (SC/ST students were already covered), over five years 2025-26 to 2029-30.

questions.subject: Education policy
questions.q: Maharashtra waived examination fees for how many Class XI-XII students in Latur district as drought relief (announced 13 Oct 2026)?
questions.e: Exam fees of 82,074 Class XI and XII students in Latur district were waived as part of drought relief measures.

questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.q: Which is India’s first 100% literate Union Territory, declared in October 2026?
questions.e: Lakshadweep became India’s first 100% literate UT under the ULLAS adult-literacy programme.

questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.q: ULLAS stands for:
o: Unified Learning and Literacy Assessment Scheme
Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society
Universal Library and Learning Access System
Upliftment through Literacy and Academic Support
questions.e: ULLAS = Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society, the national adult-education scheme.

questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.q: The National SARAS Mela 2026, graced by President Droupadi Murmu, was held in:
questions.e: The National SARAS Mela 2026 was held at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, on 15 October 2026.

questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.q: The Lakhpati Didi initiative is aimed at:
questions.e: Lakhpati Didi supports women entrepreneurs of Self-Help Groups in building sustainable livelihoods.

questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.q: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan was launched on:
questions.e: PM GatiShakti was launched on 13 October 2021 and completed five years in October 2026.

  • No: negative marking

  • Language I: 30 questions

capsules.subject: Teaching
capsules.title: IIT Bombay: 30 ad hoc counsellors at the Student Wellness Centre (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: IIT Bombay invited applications for 30 ad hoc counsellor posts at its Student Wellness Centre — 26 student counsellors and 4 senior counsellors — with applications closing 17 October 2026 and interviews 12–18 October. Candidates need an MA/MSc in Psychology (clinical/counselling/social) with 55%+, two years' post-qualification experience for student counsellors and ten years for senior counsellors. The drive follows the 18 September 2026 death of a second-year BTech student and campus protests over mental-health support for nearly 14,000 students. Appointments are initially for 89 days, joining from 15 October.

capsules.subject: Recruitment
capsules.title: BPSC TRE 4.0: 33,320 teacher posts; last date 26 October 2026
capsules.body: The Bihar Public Service Commission has increased BPSC TRE 4.0 (Advt 15/2026) vacancies from 32,388 to 33,320 school-teacher posts for classes 1–12 (announced 7 October 2026). Apply online 25 September – 26 October 2026 at bpsc.bih.nic.in. Qualification: graduation/post-graduation in the subject plus B.Ed / STET / CTET / D.El.Ed. Age (as on 01.01.2026): 18–37 (UR male), 40 (UR female, BC, EBC), 42 (SC/ST). Fee: ₹750 (General/OBC/EWS), ₹200 (Bihar SC/ST, domicile women, PwD). Selection: written examination + document verification. Pay: Level 6–9 (₹25,000–₹32,000/month).

capsules.subject: Eligibility Test
capsules.title: Bihar STET 2026: 2nd dummy admit card released 1 October
capsules.body: The Bihar School Examination Board released the 2nd dummy admit card for Bihar STET 2026 (Secondary Teacher Eligibility Test, Advt P.R.183/2026) on 1 October 2026, with corrections open during 1–7 October 2026 at stetregistration.cbrt.co.in. The computer-based test covers classes 9–12. Fee: ₹960 (one paper) / ₹1,440 (both papers) for UR/EWS/BC/EBC; ₹760/₹1,140 for SC/ST/PwD. Qualifying STET (or CTET) is required for BPSC TRE 4.0 applicants.

capsules.subject: Education policy
capsules.title: Odisha approves free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students (13 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Odisha Cabinet on 13 October 2026 approved free textbooks for ~28.7 lakh Class 9-10 students of government and aided secondary schools — extending coverage beyond SC/ST students who already received them. The Rs 284.07-crore scheme runs five years (2025-26 to 2029-30) with procurement through a transparent competitive process under the Odisha General Financial Rules.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: Lakshadweep becomes India’s first 100% literate Union Territory
capsules.body: Lakshadweep has been declared India’s first 100% literate Union Territory under ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society), the national programme for adult literacy and lifelong learning under the Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: President Murmu to grace National SARAS Mela 2026 in Vijayawada
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu visited Andhra Pradesh on 14–15 October 2026 and graced the National SARAS Mela 2026 at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada, reviewing rural products and interacting with women entrepreneurs of Self-Help Groups under the Lakhpati Didi initiative.
